### TypeScript presets

`@workerstack/repo/tsconfig/*` holds the shared `tsconfig` files: `base`, `strict`, `bun`, `web` and `worker`.

```json
{ "extends": "@workerstack/repo/tsconfig/bun", "include": ["**/*.ts"] }
```

### Commit messages

The generated `commit-msg` hook (`bun repo commit-msg`) holds a message to its subject plus at most three more things. Anything else is refused, and each refusal names the fix:

| Refused | Passes instead |
| --- | --- |
| a `Key: value` line (`Co-Authored-By: A <a@b.c>`, `Signed-off-by:`, `Why: x`) | a plain sentence for a why |
| an attribution: `🤖`, `noreply@anthropic.com`, or a line starting `Generated with` | nothing; the work is the author's (a subject that says "generated with" passes) |
| a `Breaking:` line | a `BREAKING CHANGE: <what breaks>` footer (the line and the non-blank lines after it) |
| any other body line | nothing: subject only |
| a commit over `commit.maxChangedLines` with no body line | one line saying why, even beside a footer |
| two or more why-lines over the limit | one line |

Allowed besides the subject: a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer, git's revert line `This reverts commit <sha>.` (7 to 40 hex digits), and, only over the size limit, one why-line. Merge commits pass. The subject takes the types `feat fix perf refactor test docs build ci chore revert`, with `!` before the colon for a breaking change; a plan's `commit:` line takes the same list.

On Linux, `git commit --amend` (an alias for it too) is judged as the whole commit it makes: the size limit, the test and CHANGELOG rules and red-proof read the change from `HEAD^`, not only the newly staged lines. Elsewhere an amend is judged on its staged lines, as a plain commit is.

```console
$ git commit -m "feat: add x" -m "Co-Authored-By: A <a@b.c>"
commit-msg: the message was refused
  - remove "Co-Authored-By: A <a@b.c>"; commits carry no Key: value lines (write a why as a plain sentence)
```

### Push

`bun repo push [<branch>]` pushes a branch and waits on its ci run with `bun repo ci wait`. Without a branch it picks one: the default branch is `origin/HEAD`; the recent branches are those in the last 30 reflog entries and the 8 newest heads that were committed to within 7 days, minus the default branch and `wt/*`.

| On | Result |
| --- | --- |
| a `wt/*` branch | exit 1: run `bun repo worktree finish <name>` from the root, then `bun repo push` there |
| another non-default branch | pushes it |
| the default branch, no recent branch | pushes the default branch |
| the default branch, one recent branch | pushes that branch |
| the default branch, several | exit 5, naming them: run `bun repo push <branch>` |
| a detached HEAD, or no `origin` default branch | exit 4 (`git remote set-head origin --auto` for the latter) |

A branch with no upstream is pushed with `git push -u origin <branch>`. The push runs through the pre-push hook and shows its output. Exit codes: 0 passed, 1 failed (a refused push, a worktree branch, or a failed ci run), 2 superseded, 3 nothing to wait on, 4 error (also a bad argument: `usage: repo push [<branch>]`), 5 ask. After the push, 0 to 4 are `bun repo ci wait`'s.

### Bench

The `benchmark` pack also links the `/benchmark` skill, which picks the dimensions and writes the spec.

`bun repo bench <name>` runs `.repo/bench/<name>.bench.ts`, whose default export is `defineBench` from `@workerstack/repo/bench` (with the types `BenchSpec`, `BenchCandidate`, `BenchMetric`, `Better` and `OsLabel`):

```ts
import { defineBench } from "@workerstack/repo/bench";

export default defineBench({
  candidates: { bun: { run: ["bun", "x.ts"] }, node: { run: ["node", "x.mjs"], setup: ["bun", "build", "x.ts"] } },
  metrics: { ops: { better: "higher", unit: "ops/s", weight: 1 }, rss: { weight: 1 }, wall: { weight: 2 } },
  os: ["ubuntu-latest", "macos-latest", "windows-latest"],
  runs: 10,
  warmup: 1,
});
```

| Field | Takes |
| --- | --- |
| `candidates` | at least one name (`a-z`, `0-9`, `-`) → `run` (the command, measured) and optional `setup` (run once before, unmeasured) |
| `metrics` | at least one name → `weight` over 0, `better` `lower` (default) or `higher`, optional `unit` |
| `runs` | measured runs per candidate, at least 3; default 10 |
| `warmup` | unmeasured runs per candidate first; default 1 |
| `os` | runner labels `--remote` measures on: `ubuntu-latest`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, `macos-latest`, `macos-13`, `windows-latest`; default none |

Built in, lower is better, weight only: `wall` (ms), `cpu` (ms, user plus system) and `rss` (MB, peak). Any other metric is read from the candidate's last stdout line, `bench: {"ops": 9120}`; a run without it fails. Candidates run interleaved, round-robin. Each candidate's score is the weighted mean, over metrics, of best/value (value/best when higher is better) on medians, × 100, so the best on every metric scores 100; medians are raised to a floor first (wall 0.1 ms, cpu 1 ms, rss 1 MB, custom 1e-6), so a 0 never divides. Each cell is `median ±CV% min–max`; a CV over 10% gets `!` and a line naming the cause. On Linux a child's peak RSS starts from the runner's own (the kernel carries it across exec), so the env records that peak as `rssFloorBytes` (null on macOS and Windows, which count per process), and an rss median within 5% of it gets `~` and a line saying the real peak is at most that. Columns go by weight, then name; rows by score, then name. The raw samples, machine and commit go to `.repo/tmp/bench/<name>/<os label>.json`.

```console
$ bun repo bench startup
startup · ubuntu-latest (linux x64) · AMD Ryzen 9 7950X (32) · 64 GB · bun 1.3.2 · 82c0e43+dirty · 10 runs, 1 warmup
candidate  score  wall ms (×2)       ops ops/s (×1)      rss MB (×1)
bun          100  41.2 ±4% 39–45     9120 ±3% 8700–9500  48.1 ±1% 47–49
node          62  88.0 ±11%! 76–104  7010 ±4% 6600–7400  61.3 ±1% 60–63
! node wall: CV 11% over 10%; rerun with more runs or a quieter machine (load from other work counts)
raw: .repo/tmp/bench/startup/ubuntu-latest.json
```

`--remote` also measures on the spec's other `os` labels in CI: it runs here first when this machine's label is listed, dispatches `bench.yml` (the `benchmark` pack) at HEAD's sha, waits up to 90 minutes, downloads each `bench-<name>-<os>` artifact and prints one table per OS. It refuses, one line each: no `.github/workflows/bench.yml`, bench.yml not on `origin/<default branch>` (GitHub dispatches only from there), HEAD not on origin, a dirty tree, and an `os` with no other label. Exit codes: 0 done, 1 a candidate or the remote run failed, 4 a bad argument, spec or precondition.

### Evals

`bun repo eval <name>` runs `evals/<name>/eval.ts` on Claude. It first prints a worst-case estimate and refuses a run over the cap before any call. The cap is $1.00 by default; `--max-cost <usd>` raises it. `--dry-run` stops after the estimate and reads no key. `--via session` (the default) runs each call as `claude -p` on the Claude Code session you are logged in to, with no key; Claude Code adds about 1500 hidden input tokens to every call, which the estimate counts, and a reply may pass the max tokens, so a run can overshoot the cap by the last case's extra output. Without the `claude` CLI logged in it prints `eval: --via session needs the claude CLI, logged in; install Claude Code, or use --via api` and exits 1. `--via api` calls the Anthropic API and needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; any other `--via` value exits 4 (`eval: --via takes session or api`). A real run stops before a case that could cross the cap, caches each answer under `.repo/tmp/evals/cache`, so a rerun of unchanged text costs $0 (session and API answers are cached apart), and writes a spend summary under `.repo/tmp/evals/runs`.

```console
$ bun repo eval skill-routing --dry-run
eval skill-routing: 24 cases x 3 samples = 72 calls on claude-haiku-5-5 via session, at most $0.0834 (cap $1.00)
```

An eval lists the repo files and folders its prompt and grader read as `files` in `defineEval`: repo-relative, with `/`, and each must exist, or the eval is refused (`eval broken: files.0: no file or folder agents/skills/nope`). `--changed <base>` runs every case of the eval when one of those, or anything under `evals/<name>/`, changed since the merge base with `<base>`, committed or not, and runs none otherwise (exit 0, no call made). `evals/rules-compliance` asks `claude-sonnet-5-5` its first step for real prompts, given the rules and the scope page, 2 samples a case so its bound stays under the $1.00 cap; both evals pass an answer whose first word is the expected one.

```console
$ bun repo eval skill-routing --changed main --dry-run
eval skill-routing: agents/skills/su/SKILL.md changed since main
eval skill-routing: 24 cases x 3 samples = 72 calls on claude-haiku-5-5 via session, at most $0.0834 (cap $1.00)
$ bun repo eval rules-compliance --changed main
eval rules-compliance: nothing it reads changed since main
```

With the `evals` pack on, `bun repo github` keeps a GitHub environment named `evals` that needs one reviewer and deploys only from the default branch, and sync writes `.github/workflows/eval.yml`. It runs only when started by hand, with the eval's name and a cap in US dollars (default 1) and `via`, `session` (default) or `api`. Its one job runs in the `evals` environment, so it waits for your approval and reads the secret from there: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` for `session`, which installs `@anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.323` first, or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for `api`. It restores and saves the answer cache, and uploads the summaries as the `eval-<name>` artifact.

```console
$ claude setup-token                                   # prints a long-lived token; copy it
$ gh secret set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN --env evals    # once, for --via session; paste the token
$ gh secret set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY --env evals          # once, only for --via api; also set a spend limit in the Anthropic console
$ gh workflow run eval.yml -f eval=skill-routing -f max-cost=0.5 -f via=session
```

The run then waits under "Review deployments" until you approve it. A dispatch from any branch but the default one is refused by the environment.

### Env

`@workerstack/repo/env` exports `defineEnv` and `sealed` (with the types `EnvConfig`, `EnvInstance`, `ProcessSpec`, `Scope`, `Sealed` and `Value`). It is for scripts: a Cloudflare Worker reads `ctx.env`, and `defineEnv` there throws the message "repo env: defineEnv is script-only; a Cloudflare Worker reads ctx.env".

```ts
import { defineEnv, sealed } from "@workerstack/repo/env";

export const repoEnv = defineEnv({
  global: { CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: "28fa2622…", NPM_TOKEN: sealed("YWdlLWVuY3J5cHRpb24ub3Jn…") },
  local: {},
  dev: {},
  prod: {},
  process: { CI: "optional", HOME: "required" },
});

repoEnv.current.NPM_TOKEN; // string, decrypted on the first sealed read
repoEnv.process.HOME; // string; CI is a key only when set (string | undefined)
```

| Field | Takes |
| --- | --- |
| `global` | values every scope shares; optional |
| `local` `dev` `prod` | one block per scope (required, may be `{}`); a string or `sealed(...)` per key |
| `process` | process variables this env reads → `"required"` (a string; throws when read unset) or `"optional"` (a key only when set, typed `?: string \| undefined`, so a spread over defaults keeps them) |
| `parent` | another `defineEnv` result; its values carry into each scope |

A scope merges in this order: own `global`, then the parent's scope view, then own scope; the later wins. `global` is the parent's `global` then own. The instance holds:

| Member | Reads |
| --- | --- |
| `current` | the scope `REPO_ENV` names (`local`, `dev` or `prod`; `local` when unset), checked at each read; a key that scope lacks throws |
| `global` `local` `dev` `prod` | that view's merged values |
| `process` | the declared process variables, read from `process.env` at each read |
| `read(source)` | the `process` view of another `source` object (a test seam) |
| `sealedKeys(scope)` | the set of keys whose winning value in `scope` is sealed |

`sealed("<base64>")` takes the base64 of an age cipher made for the recipient in `.repo/env.keys.json` (`{ "recipient": "age1…", "repo": "<name>" }`); plaintext or an empty string throws at once. Nothing decrypts until a sealed value is read: the first such read decrypts every sealed value of the env and its parents in one `bun` child and keeps the plaintext in that instance only, so a plain read needs no key. The key is `WORKERSTACK_ENV_KEY` (an age identity) when set, else every `~/.workerstack/keys/*.key`; the repo's own is `~/.workerstack/keys/<repo>.key`, saved at 0600.

#### Commands

`bun repo env <verb>` seals, lists, reads and hands out the values of the `defineEnv` files, so no `age` CLI or base64 is needed. A value never enters argv: `set` reads a piped stdin whole (one trailing newline dropped) or, on a TTY, a hidden prompt.

```console
$ bun repo env init                                # rerun with the same key: repo env: already set up (acme)
repo env: wrote .repo/env.keys.json (recipient age1qz…) and ~/.workerstack/keys/acme.key (0600); back the key up in a password manager
$ echo "$v" | bun repo env set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY --scope prod      # --file <env file> picks the file
repo env: sealed prod.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY in projects/shop/env.ts
$ echo acme.io | bun repo env set APEX_DOMAIN --scope global --plain
repo env: wrote global.APEX_DOMAIN (plain) in projects/shop/env.ts
$ bun repo env ls
KEY                SCOPE   KIND    FILE                   USED BY
APEX_DOMAIN        global  plain   projects/shop/env.ts   projects/shop/deploy.ts
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY  prod    sealed  projects/shop/env.ts   projects/shop/deploy.ts, projects/shop/seed.ts
$ bun repo env get STRIPE_SECRET_KEY --scope prod                  # --reveal prints it whole
sk_test_51…••••
$ bun repo env run --scope prod -- wrangler deploy                 # values reach that child's env only
$ bun repo env export --scope dev --format dotenv
APEX_DOMAIN='acme.io'
$ pbpaste | bun repo env key import                # rerun: repo env: already set up (acme)
repo env: saved ~/.workerstack/keys/acme.key (0600); it unlocks .repo/env.keys.json's recipient
$ bun repo env key ci --dry-run
repo env: would run: gh secret set WORKERSTACK_ENV_KEY (the key on stdin)
```

| Verb | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `init` | writes `.repo/env.keys.json` and the key `~/.workerstack/keys/<repo>.key` (0600); the repo is named by the main checkout's folder, so a worktree names the same repo; the same key again prints `already set up`, a key file for another recipient is refused |
| `set KEY --scope s` | seals the value read from stdin into the env file's `s` block in place (or writes it plain with `--plain`; `--scope global` writes `global`), keeps every other byte, adds the `sealed` import when missing, and writes through a temp file and rename |
| `get KEY --scope s` | prints the value masked (first 10 characters, then `…••••`; `••••` under 12 characters); `--reveal` prints it whole |
| `ls` | one row per key: `KEY`, `SCOPE`, `KIND` (`plain` or `sealed`), `FILE` and `USED BY` (the tracked files that import the env file and name the key) |
| `run --scope s -- cmd` | runs `cmd` with the scope's values in its env only and passes its exit code through; `WORKERSTACK_ENV_KEY` is not handed to the child |
| `export --scope s --format dotenv` | prints the scope's values sorted, one `KEY=value` line each, quoted so dotenv and Bun's `--env-file` read them back: single quotes when the value has no `'`, else double quotes with only `\n` and `\r` escaped, else backticks |
| `key import` | reads an age identity from stdin, checks it unlocks the recipient in `.repo/env.keys.json` and saves it as `~/.workerstack/keys/<repo>.key` (0600); the same key again prints `already set up` |
| `key ci [--dry-run]` | sets the `WORKERSTACK_ENV_KEY` secret through `gh`, with the key on gh's stdin; of several keys it picks the one matching the recipient; `--dry-run` prints the line it would run |

The env file is `--file` when given, else the env files that declare the key, else the one env file in the repo. `export` refuses a value that has a `$` (Bun expands it in every quote, dotenv in none) or that no quote holds: `<KEY> has no dotenv quoting that bun and dotenv read back the same; pass it with \`bun repo env run\``. A bad verb or flag prints `usage: bun repo env init | set KEY --scope <global|local|dev|prod> [--plain] [--file f] | get KEY --scope s [--reveal] | ls | run --scope s -- cmd | export --scope s --format dotenv | key import | key ci [--dry-run]` on stderr and exits 4. A refusal is one line, exit 1:

```console
repo env: no defineEnv file declares STRIPE_SECRET_KEY; pass --file <env file>
repo env: 2 env files: a/env.ts, b/env.ts; pass --file
repo env: no .repo/env.keys.json; run `bun repo env init`
repo env: the pasted key does not unlock age1qz…; paste this repo's key
repo env: init found ~/.workerstack/keys/acme.key for another recipient; move it aside first
```

The runtime errors, one line each (`<key>` is the read, `<repo>` the name in `.repo/env.keys.json`):

```console
repo env: REPO_ENV is "staging"; set it to local, dev or prod
repo env: NPM_TOKEN has no prod value in src/env.ts; add it to its prod block
repo env: process.HOME is required and unset
repo env: NPM_TOKEN is sealed and no key is at ~/.workerstack/keys/<repo>.key; run `bun repo env key import`
repo env: NPM_TOKEN is sealed for another key than ~/.workerstack/keys/<repo>.key; run `bun repo env key import` with this repo's key
repo env: NPM_TOKEN could not be decrypted: <reason>
```

`bun repo check` reads every tracked `.ts`, `.tsx` and `.mts` file that calls `defineEnv(` and fails, one line each:

```console
env: src/env.ts global.NPM_TOKEN looks like a secret (credential name) but is plain; run `bun repo env set NPM_TOKEN --scope global`
env: src/env.ts dev.NPM_TOKEN is missing (prod has it); add it to dev or remove it from prod
env: src/env.ts reads process.env.HOME but its process block does not declare it; add `HOME: "optional"`
```

The reason is `sk_ prefix` (or another provider prefix), `high entropy` or `credential name`; `pk_live_` and `pk_test_` values pass. A scope block with a spread or no key takes no part in the missing-key rule. The check also reads a config held in a same-file const, through `as const`, `satisfies` or parentheses (`const config = { … } as const; defineEnv(config)`).

### Agents and references

`@workerstack/repo/agents/*` holds the stock skills, rules, subagents and hooks that `bun repo sync` links into each host tree. `@workerstack/repo/references/*` holds these files, which a repo's own `references/INDEX.md` links in `node_modules`.

A subagent source may carry `variants:`, a list of mappings. One source renders one subagent per entry, each entry deep-merging over the source's frontmatter without `variants`. Every entry needs a `name`, which names its file:

```yaml
variants:
  - name: implementer-deep
    claudecode:
      model: opus
  - name: implementer-fast
    claudecode:
      model: sonnet
tier: implementer
```

## Fast plan format (SSOT)

A short checklist for work the person chose to do fast. Saved by `cli/scripts/persist-fast-plan.ts`. Default is a plan (`plan-format.md`).

### Path

`.repo/plans-fast/{serial}-{slug}-{YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ}.md`, named like a plan.

### Frontmatter

`serial`, `name`, `status` (`ready | in-progress | done | blocked`), `created`, `source`, and optional `commit:`. No `strategy`, no `reviews`.

### Body

The first line is `FAST_PLAN_NAME: <name>`, then `commit:`, then `# {slug}`, then `## Goal`, `## Steps`, `## Verify`, in that order, then an optional `## Previous mistakes`. Steps and Verify are flat `N [ ] text` boxes; a new plan has only `[ ]`. No review, so `in-progress` needs none.

### Cap and denials

At most 40 lines, frontmatter included; `## Previous mistakes` and its lines are outside the cap. It is append-only, and under `/away` it holds the `- decision:` lines. Replies:

- `a fast plan has no strategy`
- `a fast plan holds only Goal, Steps and Verify, then an optional Previous mistakes`
- `a fast plan is at most 40 lines; write a plan (/write-plan-deep)`
- `a new fast plan has only [ ] boxes`

### Approval

All-fast block: header `fast-plan {n}`, rows `i implement`, `h hand off`, `or reply to revise`. It has no strategy codes. `i` runs `/implement-plan-fast {n}`; `h` hands off with `/implement-plan-fast {n}` as Next.

A fast roadmap (`fast-roadmap-format.md`) runs its slices as fast plans.

## Fast roadmap format (SSOT)

A short ordered program of fast plans, for work the person chose to do fast. Saved by `cli/scripts/persist-fast-roadmap.ts`. Default is a roadmap (`roadmap-format.md`).

### Path

`.repo/roadmaps-fast/{serial}-{slug}-{YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ}.md`. Serials count in `roadmaps-fast` only.

### Frontmatter

`serial`, `name`, `status` (`draft | locked | in-progress | done`), `created`, `source`. No `strategy`, no `reviews`.

### Body

The first line is `FAST_ROADMAP_NAME: <name>`, then `# {slug}`, then `## Order` and `## Verify`, in that order, then an optional `## Previous mistakes`. Order has two or more slices, `N [ ] title: sentence`; Verify is flat `N [ ] text` boxes numbered after the slices. A new roadmap has only `[ ]`.

### Cap and Location

At most 20 lines, frontmatter included; Location lines and `## Previous mistakes` with its lines are not counted. Previous mistakes is append-only and holds the `- decision:` lines under `/away`. A slice may carry an indented `Location: <abs path>` line: an absolute path to a fast plan under `.repo/plans-fast/`.

### Denials

- `a fast roadmap has no strategy`
- `a fast roadmap holds only Order and Verify, then an optional Previous mistakes`
- `a fast roadmap is at most 20 lines; write a roadmap (/write-roadmap-deep)`
- `a fast roadmap has two or more slices; write a fast plan (/write-plan-fast)`
- `a new fast roadmap has only [ ] boxes`
- `a fast roadmap slice's Location is a fast plan under .repo/plans-fast/`

### Approval

Block: header `fast-roadmap {n}`, rows `i implement`, `h hand off`, `or reply to revise`. No strategy codes. `i` sets `status: locked`, then runs `/implement-roadmap-fast {n}`; `h` hands off with that as Next.

### Run

`/implement-roadmap-fast {n}` refuses a draft, sets `in-progress`, runs `/write-plan-fast` then `/implement-plan-fast` per open slice (no stop between), ticks each slice after its plan, runs Verify and sets `done`.

## google-workspace

Create and edit Google Sheets, Docs, Slides, Calendar events, and Gmail from the session.

```
bun repo google-workspace whoami
bun repo google-workspace scopes
bun repo google-workspace login
bun repo google-workspace sheet create --title "Q3" --csv "item,qty\nA,2"
bun repo google-workspace sheet set --id ID --cell A1 --value x
bun repo google-workspace sheet get --id ID --range A1:B10
bun repo google-workspace sheet append --id ID --csv "c,3"
bun repo google-workspace sheet clear --id ID --range A1:Z
bun repo google-workspace doc create --title "Notes" --body "hello"
bun repo google-workspace doc append --id ID --body "more"
bun repo google-workspace drive list --query "mimeType='application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet'"
bun repo google-workspace slide create --title "Deck"
bun repo google-workspace meeting create --title "Standup" --start 2026-09-15T09:00:00Z --end 2026-09-15T09:15:00Z --attendees a@x.com,b@y.com
bun repo google-workspace mail send --to you@example.com --subject hi --body hello
bun repo google-workspace mail list
```

Each person has their own Google Cloud app. Creds stay in `~/.workerstack/` on that machine. Do not share OAuth JSON or tokens. Do not commit them. Inviting others to a meeting is attendee emails, not shared creds.

Handheld (any OS): `bun repo setup google-workspace` or `bun repo setup` → google-workspace. Opens each Cloud Console page, waits, copies the Desktop JSON into `~/.workerstack/workspace/default/google-oauth.json`, then browser Allow. Non-TTY: `--creds PATH` to a Desktop download. `--account NAME` for a second Google user.

Doctor reports google-workspace as optional: `ok` when Desktop OAuth JSON, tokens, gcloud ADC, or `~/.clasprc.json` exists, else `missing (optional)`. It prints source names (`oauth` `tokens` `adc` `clasprc`), not secrets. `clasprc` is Drive-only.

Two Google accounts on one machine: `--account NAME` (or `WORKSPACE_ACCOUNT`). Each account, `default` included, uses `~/.workerstack/workspace/NAME/`.

```
bun repo google-workspace --account work login
bun repo google-workspace --account work whoami
bun repo google-workspace accounts
```

Each account needs its own Desktop JSON in that folder (`google-oauth.json`) and its own `login`.

Clasp’s public OAuth client is Drive-only. Calendar and Gmail are restricted; Google blocks extra scopes on that app. Use **your** Desktop OAuth client.

### Agent: setup e2e

If `whoami` works but `meeting` / `mail` / `sheet set` fail with missing scope or “app is blocked”, run **this user** through `bun repo setup google-workspace` (TTY). Do not reuse another person’s JSON. Do not invent a client JSON.

Local dir is created by setup (`~/.workerstack/`, mode 700 on Unix). Manual equivalent: `mkdir -p "$HOME/.workerstack" && chmod 700 "$HOME/.workerstack"` then:

1. Open `https://console.cloud.google.com/projectcreate` — **Create**. Org can be their Workspace org. Note **Project ID** from the dashboard URL (`?project=`).
2. Open `https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/overview/create?project=PROJECT_ID` (or **Google Auth Platform → Branding**).
   - App name: anything (`autorun` is fine). That string is only the Allow screen.
   - User support email: their address.
   - Audience: **Internal** if the Google account is a paid Workspace org (e.g. `@rearm.co`). **Testing** + add their own address as a test user if it is a personal `@gmail.com` (Internal is not offered). APIs work on both; only this consent type changes.
   - Next / Create through the wizard.
3. Open `https://console.cloud.google.com/flows/enableapi?apiid=calendar-json.googleapis.com,gmail.googleapis.com,sheets.googleapis.com,docs.googleapis.com,drive.googleapis.com&project=PROJECT_ID` — **Enable**.
4. Open `https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/clients/create?project=PROJECT_ID`.
   - Application type: **Desktop app**.
   - Create → **Download JSON**.
5. Copy the download to `$HOME/.workerstack/workspace/default/google-oauth.json` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.workerstack\workspace\default\google-oauth.json`). chmod 600 on Unix. Confirm it has `"installed"` and `client_id`. For `--account NAME`, use `$HOME/.workerstack/workspace/NAME/google-oauth.json`.
6. From the repo: `bun repo google-workspace login` (or `--account NAME`) — browser Allow. Tokens write beside the JSON (`workspace/NAME/tokens.json`).
7. Smoke:

```
bun repo google-workspace whoami
bun repo google-workspace scopes
bun repo google-workspace sheet create --title smoke-sheet --csv "k,v\nok,1"
bun repo google-workspace doc create --title smoke-doc --body ok
bun repo google-workspace slide create --title smoke-slide
bun repo google-workspace meeting create --title smoke-meeting --start 2026-09-16T09:00:00Z --end 2026-09-16T09:15:00Z
bun repo google-workspace mail send --to THEIR_EMAIL --subject smoke --body ok
```

`scopes` must include `calendar`, `gmail.modify` or `gmail.send`, `spreadsheets`, `documents`, `drive`. If login times out, they did not finish Allow; re-run `login`.

If `google-oauth.json` is missing, `login` prints `setup: bun repo setup google-workspace`. Prefer the handheld setup (it opens the Project ID URLs). Manual steps above still work.

`gcloud` on PATH is an alternate login (`gcloud auth application-default login` with the extra scopes). Still per person, still local.

## Hooks

SessionStart carries only the folder map: Claude / Codex run the `session-map` hook, which injects the code-only map `bun repo map` prints as `additionalContext` (capped under Claude Code's 10,000-char per-hook `additionalContext` limit, about 2.4k tokens, below the 5k `bun repo map` budget; cache-stable, fail-open) and logs `{rows, tokens}` to `.repo/tmp/sessions/<sid>/map.json`. Inject nothing else at SessionStart. Antigravity has no generated sessionStart. Do not register a SessionStart hook on `.grok/hooks/orchestrate-parent.json`.

Grok PostToolUse / SessionStart are observe-only — do not attempt output scrub; compress via RTK / spawn / isolation facts only. Do not add PostToolUse scrub hooks. UserPromptSubmit may emit a one-line `sessionGate=ask|away` plus session receipt, then up to 8 other live lines from `~/.workerstack/board/` (`hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`). The current session's own line is omitted. Skip host Stop banners. `/ask` and `/away` exact-match slashes stamp `session-gate-{sid}` to `ask` or `away`. Sid-less: no stamp. Default: `ask`. The `sessionGate=` word is the effective mode: the stamp wins, else the newest `in-progress` plan or roadmap in this session's `.repo/tmp/sessions/<sid>/approvals.txt` with a valid `mode:`, else `ask`. Another session's plans never count.

In `sessionGate=away`, parent Stop blocks a reply whose last line ends in `?` and does not end with an approval block. Reason: `away: do not ask; decide, log "- decision: {question} → {choice}, because {why}" in the plan, and continue`. The block uses the `stop-block` counter, cap 3, so a true blocker still reaches the person. Under away, once the review settles, Stop also runs the approval block's header choice (a bare `i`) for every kind (plan, roadmap, fast-plan, fast-roadmap). It logs `- decision: approval of {kind N} under /away → i (strategy S) because away runs the block's header choice once the review settled` in each file's `## Previous mistakes`, stamps `away-run`, and blocks once with `away: ran the approval block's header choice and logged it in each file so re-read each file before you edit it; i approves …`. The `away-run` stamp keeps it to one run per approval block. `sessionGate=ask` does not Stop-block.

Claude / Codex / Antigravity / Cursor PreToolUse still run the `scrub-spawn-prompt` and `gate-fat-tools` hooks. Grok spawn/fat rewrite is the `orchestrate-parent` hook. RTK stays `.grok/hooks/rtk.json`, which runs the `rtk-grok` hook.
Every repo hook command finds the root (`$GROK_WORKSPACE_ROOT`, else `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, else its git top level) and runs `<root>/node_modules/.bin/repo hook <name>`. A checkout with no install prints `repo: <root>/node_modules/.bin/repo is missing; run bun install` and exits 1, which never blocks the tool call. `bun repo sync --check` fails any repo hook in another form.
Claude Code's `WorktreeCreate` and `WorktreeRemove` come from the `claudecode` block of `hooks.jsonc` and run the `worktree` hook (60s), so its worktrees land in `.worktrees/<name>` on `wt/<name>`. Other harnesses have no such event and call `bun repo worktree add` directly.

### Cursor

`cursor-agent` reads `.cursor/hooks.json` (JSONC, `version: 1`, camelCase events `preToolUse` `beforeSubmitPrompt` `stop` `sessionStart`, flat `{command, timeout, matcher}` entries). `bun repo sync` writes it (`cli/sync/agents/render-hooks.ts`) from `hooks.jsonc` with the matchers untranslated, so the gate and orchestrate-parent matchers name Cursor's tools (`Shell`, `Read`, `Write`, `Grep`) beside the others. `hooks-union.ts` appends a consumer's autorun scripts to it as flat entries (`Write` is Cursor's write matcher). Cursor also reads `.claude/settings.json` hooks and drops a command it already has in its own file, so nothing runs twice. Cursor refuses a hook file with a symlink on its path: keep `.cursor/` a real dir. It reads `AGENTS.md`, so there is no `.cursor/rules`. `bun repo sync` generates `.cursor` in each consumer (gitignored there); it is not in the package `files`.

Payload: `cursor_version`, `session_id`, `model`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `cwd`; no `turn_id`, no `subagent_type` (every Cursor call counts as the parent). `gate-fat-tools.ts` `harnessOf` tests a string `cursor_version` first, because `session_id` and `model` also match the Codex check. Tools the gate answers:

| Tool | Input | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Shell` | `command`, `cwd` | denylist, `.gitignore`, `git worktree add` and main-checkout git guards; dump, search, `curl` and `ls` rewrites |
| `Read` | `file_path` | denylist, 200KB deny, re-read deny |
| `Grep` | `pattern`, `file_path`, `glob` | denylist |
| `Write` | `file_path`, `content` | main-checkout deny, redirect of `.repo` work files and scratch to the root `.repo`, `.gitignore` guard; orchestrate-parent persists plans and the like |

`Read` takes no offset or limit and `Grep` no `head_limit`, so the gate injects and caps neither (`limits: false` in `TOOLS.cursor`). A re-read of a file this session wrote therefore cannot say "Read with offset+limit": Cursor's reason names `bun repo job --job exec --query 'sed -n 1,200p <file>'`. `List` and `Delete` get no answer.

Reply: a deny is `{"permission":"deny","user_message":reason,"agent_message":reason}`. A rewrite is Claude's nested `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","updatedInput":{...}}}` with no `permission` and no top-level field (Cursor reads the nested form only then; `permission` would also auto-approve). Cursor applies a rewritten `command` (Shell) and `file_path` (Write), but writes its own `content`: a persisted tmp write lands at the `.repo/scratch/` path with its `TMP_NAME:` line still in the body. Empty stdout with exit 0 allows. Invalid JSON on stdout blocks the call. `stop` may reply `{"decision":"block","reason":...}`. orchestrate-parent handles Cursor's `beforeSubmitPrompt` only to write `git-asked.json` (see Worktrees); there it stamps no `/ask` or `/away`, handles no `y` or `h`, prints no board line and adds no context.

Session agent tools are on. Fat Read/Grep/Glob/Bash still gate. Writes under `.repo/plans/`, `.repo/plans-fast/` (a fast plan the person asked for: `fast-plan-format.md`; no review, no strategy, its block is `fast-plan {n}` with `i` and `h` only), `.repo/roadmaps-fast/` (a fast roadmap the person asked for: `fast-roadmap-format.md`; at most 20 lines, block `fast-roadmap {n}` with `i` and `h` only), `.repo/handoffs/`, `.repo/implementations/`, `.repo/roadmaps/`, and `.repo/scratch/` root files persist via `cli/scripts/persist-plan.ts` / `persist-handoff.ts` / `persist-implementation.ts` / `persist-tmp.ts` / `persist-roadmap.ts`. The hook hands the host the absolute path of the saved file. Invalid body denies. A Write of a saved plan updates that file in place (same serial); an Edit of a saved plan is checked against the text it would produce, and a valid one runs as sent. `## Previous mistakes` entries are append-only on both. Roadmaps follow the same rules: a Write of a saved roadmap is validated and the host writes it, and an Edit is checked against the text it would produce.

Writes under `.repo/lessons/` go through `bun repo lessons`: a lesson Write in a managed worktree is validated, saved, and reindexed (`INDEX.md`) there, and the same Write in the main checkout is denied with the Worktrees reason; an Edit of a lesson is denied with the Write and `lessons.ts hit` routes. Lessons match per holding checkout: the root, or the managed worktree that holds the file; an unmanaged linked worktree falls back to the caller's checkout. On any other Write or Edit, PreToolUse adds `additionalContext` for lessons whose globs match the file, each once per session (`.repo/tmp/sessions/<sid>/lessons-seen.json`). It reads the lesson files, not `INDEX.md`, and fails open.

SubagentStop (and child Stop with `subagentType`) intercepts a parseable `need:` whose jobs are all `search|exec|slice|fetch` (cap 4): runs job in-hook and continues the child with concatenated facts. Mixed/web/test, parse fail, FALLBACK, `stopHookActive`, or more than 3 intercepts per child session → empty stdout (allow stop).

Stop and SubagentStop timeout is 30s (job cap is 20s). PreToolUse / UserPromptSubmit stay at 5s.

The canonical hooks.jsonc event is `beforeSubmitPrompt` (→ Claude/Codex `UserPromptSubmit`), not `userPromptSubmit`.

`[features] two_pass_compaction` must live in `~/.grok/config.toml` (from `agents/global-settings/grok.toml` via `bun repo yolo`). Project `.grok/config.toml` cannot set `[features]`.

### Local ci and bun test

`localCiGuard` in `gate-shell.ts` denies a shell command that runs the whole ci: `bun repo ci` (also run by path or without `bun`) or `bun run ci` (npm and pnpm too), alone or in a compound, when `ci` is followed by the end or a flag. The reason is ``GitHub runs ci, not you: push the branch, then run `bun repo ci wait <branch>` in the background. To check one change, run the nearest test file with `bun run test <file>`.`` `ci wait`, `skips`, `times` and `merge` pass. `testRunGuard` rewrites `bun test` (bun's own runner, which cannot run the vitest suites) to `bun run test` for every caller, in a compound too; an implementer's or a reviewing parent's plain run then goes through `bun repo job` as before.

### Push gate

`ci-push-gate.ts` makes a turn that pushed wait for ci. On every PreToolUse, parent or subagent, `notePush` runs before `emitFat` and notes each `git push` in the Bash command: bare, `origin main`, `-u origin x`, `HEAD:refs/heads/x`, `git -C <dir> push`, `cd <dir> && git push` and chains. `bun repo push [<branch>]` notes a push of the branch they pick (an explicit branch, or the recent-branch table's); ask, a worktree branch and a detached HEAD note none. Dirs go through `path.resolve`, and the branch and sha are read in that dir. The entry lands in the session's `pushed.json` (`[{branch, sha, at}]`) and stays pending until a later hook sees the sha land on `origin/<branch>`; a rejected push and every older sha are ignored. The hook writes only `pushed.json` and its stamp. `bun repo release` pushes through git from node, not a Bash `git push`, and waits on ci itself, so the gate does not see it.

Per branch, only the newest landed sha counts. The parent's Stop blocks while that sha has no terminal record in `.repo/tmp/ci/<sha>.json` (written by `bun repo ci wait`): `passed`, `nothing` and `error` settle it, and so do three `failed` records of this session's pushes on the branch sharing a job. Another session's records do not count. The record lives under the main checkout's `.repo/tmp/ci/`, so a push from a worktree and a wait from the root meet. The three lines:

- ``Stop: you pushed <sha> to <branch> and its ci run has no result; run `bun repo ci wait <branch>` in the background and fix it if it fails``
- ``Stop: ci failed on <sha> on <branch> (<job>); fix it in a new worktree, push, and run `bun repo ci wait <branch>` in the background; if only the user can fix a job, run bun repo backlog add 'blocked: `<job>` <why>' and name that line in your reply``
- ``Stop: <job> failed 3 times on <branch> this session; report the failure and its logs to the user, then stop``

A job only the user can fix is marked in the main checkout's `.repo/backlog.md` with an open line from column 0, ``- [ ] blocked: `<job>` <why>`` (or `- [-]`), which `bun repo backlog add 'blocked: `<job>` <why>'` writes. Each line names one job, with its exact name from the run; an indented line, a `*` bullet and a backlog in a worktree do not count. A failed run whose jobs are all blocked lets the Stop go on; otherwise the failed line names only the jobs that are not blocked, and blocked jobs do not count toward three failures. A failed run with no job names is never released. Ticking the line `[x]` re-arms the gate.

The gate runs for the parent before the ask and away checks and before the `stopHookActive` pass. It has its own `push-block` stamp, capped at 6 blocks a turn and cleared on the next prompt beside `stop-block`; it is independent of the `stop-block` cap of 3, which ask and away share. A subagent's Stop is unchanged (`interceptNeed`); its pushes settle at the parent's Stop.

### Review strategy

A plan or roadmap carries `strategy: free|spawn-fast|spawn-deep` (`plan-format.md`). `free` adds nothing here. For `spawn-*` the main session reviews and an implementer agent writes (`review-loop.md`). The code is `cli/scripts/strategy.ts`, called from `gate-fat-tools.ts` and `cli/scripts/orchestrate-parent.ts`.

Stamp: a parent's save of a plan whose frontmatter holds a `spawn-*` strategy writes `.repo/tmp/sessions/<sid>/strategy.json`, which holds the plan's canonical path. A box tick on such a plan stamps too, so a resumed run in a new session stamps on its first save. A child's save stamps nothing. The gate writes it for every harness. orchestrate-parent calls `stampPlanSave` first for the plan Writes it persists itself. The stamp only points at the plan. `activeReview` reads the plan: it is active while `status` is `in-progress` and `strategy` is `spawn-*`, so `done` and `blocked` end it with no cleanup.

Deny: `reviewGuard` in `processFatTools` sits right after the worktree deny, before the write branch and the scout return. While a review is active in an enforced harness, a parent write whose target is outside the root `.tmp/` is denied. The target is judged by canonical path after the scratch rewrite, not as typed. A child, a missing `sid` and an unenforced harness are not denied. Reason: `plan {n} runs strategy {s}: this session reviews. Spawn {implementer} for product writes; the plan, the journal and .tmp/ stay writable.`

Implementer guards apply under every strategy: the spawn prompt names the worktree path, so the implementer's first Write is under `.worktrees/<name>` (the main-checkout deny holds for it too); an `implementer-*` child's write under `.repo/plans` or `.repo/implementations` is denied (`implementer writes product files and tests only; the reviewer writes the plan and the journal`), and so is a shell `git add` or `git commit` (`implementer never stages or commits; report the changed files and the reviewer stages them`).

Test runs: a plain `bun run test …` (or `vitest`, `npm test`, `pnpm test`) from an `implementer-*` child, or from a parent while a review is active, is rewritten to `<root>/node_modules/.bin/repo job --job test --query '<command>'`. The full log goes to the stash and the caller sees the failing lines. A compound command passes through.

Approval: the Stop hook blocks a reply that should ask for approval unless it ends with an approval block that names every pending item with the strategy its file holds. The block reason is `end with this block:` and the block `closingBlock` renders from the files. On the next prompt, `i` returns `i approves plan {n}: plan {n}: run /implement-plan-deep {n} (<path>)` and leaves the file alone. A code or spelled-out strategy writes that strategy into each approved plan or roadmap (validated through the persist module), and the context says to re-read the file before work. A near-miss code (`isx`, or `id` with its `s` dropped), or a strategy word within two edits of several choices approves nothing: `"{reply}" is not a choice; end with this block again:` and the block. Any other reply gets no approval context.

The approval block `closingBlock` renders, for one plan, fenced as code:

```
plan {n} · {s}
  i  implement    if · isf · isd
  h  hand off     hf · hsf · hsd
     or reply to revise
```

A queue joins header items with `, then `; the rows never change. Replies are case-insensitive, and a trailing `.` or `!` is ignored. `i`, `y`, `yes`, `go` and `do it` approve with each file's strategy, and `h` hands off with it. The codes `if`, `isf`, `isd`, `hf`, `hsf` and `hsd` match exactly. Otherwise an action (`i`, `y`, `h`, or a word within two edits of `implement` or `hand off`) may take one or two strategy words, exact or within two edits of exactly one of `free`, `spawn-fast`, `spawn-deep`, `fast` or `deep`. Only words of four or more letters are inferred, A bare strategy word with no action, or strategy words that match nothing (`i think so`), is feedback.

Settled review: a parent spawn whose prompt starts `/review-plan {n}` or `/review-roadmap {n}` records `{"plan {n}": <reviews at spawn>}` in `.repo/tmp/sessions/<sid>/reviews-open.json`, keyed by `plan {n}` or `roadmap {n}`, never by path. An item is settled when its file's `reviews` is above the recorded number, or nothing was recorded and `reviews` is at least 1. Stop blocks an approval block that names an unsettled item, before the approval and mode checks: `plan {n}'s review has not settled; wait for it, settle its findings with reviews bumped, then end with the approval block`, or on `reviews: 0`, `plan {n} has reviews: 0; run /review-plan {n} in a fresh agent first`. A Stop block fires once, so an `i` or `h` on an unsettled item is refused too: `i did not approve plan {n}: its review has not settled; wait for it, then end with the approval block again` (`h did not hand off …` for `h`). Unsettled items never count as pending.

Handoff: `h` keeps each file's strategy; `hf`, `hsf` and `hsd` (or `h` with a strategy word) write that strategy through the same validated write as an `i` code. The hook writes one handoff for the whole block through `persistHandoff`: H1 `run-plan-{n}` (or `run-{kind}-{n}-then-…`), Goal names the items, State their paths and strategies, Context the source session, Next one leaf per item in order (`/implement-plan-deep {n}`, or `set status locked, then /implement-roadmap-deep {n}`), Watch-outs `(none)`. The context: `h handed off plan {n} (strategy spawn-fast written) to <abs path>; tell the person to run /pickup {serial} in a fresh session, and do no work here`.

Enforcement, from the live probe of each harness's child payload:

| Harness | Child marker | Enforced |
| --- | --- | --- |
| claude | `agent_type` and `agent_id` | yes |
| codex | `agent_type` and `agent_id`; shares the parent's `session_id` | yes |
| grok | `subagentType`, own `sessionId`; `harnessOf` reports `claude` | yes, through `claude` |
| antigravity | none; only a different `conversationId`, its only session-id key | no |
| cursor | none; only a different `session_id` | no |

An unenforced harness follows the rule as an instruction (`review-loop.md`). Cursor's `beforeSubmitPrompt` writes only `git-asked.json` in orchestrate-parent, so `i`, the codes and `h` have no effect there and no slash stamps: `/away` is prompt-only in Cursor, though a saved `mode: away` still runs Cursor's Stop. Antigravity has no Stop hook, so the settled-review, away and approval-run rules are prompt-only there. Headless `cursor-agent -p` (v2026.11.05) never fires `beforeSubmitPrompt`, so no prompt can grant a git subcommand there and the git denies still apply; the Cursor IDE was not tested.

`git-asked.json` (Worktrees) is keyed by sid. Claude and Codex children share the parent's sid and so its grant; a Grok, Cursor or Antigravity child has its own sid and gets none. Antigravity has no `git-asked.json`: the gate reads `lastUserInput` from the tool call, and an agy subagent's calls carry an empty one, so a child gets no grant.

Main-session compaction window: a user setting, `modelSettings.<model>.autoCompactWindow` in `~/.claude/settings.json`. Each agent carries its own value in its `claudecode` block. Do not set `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`: it overrides every agent's value.

### Worktrees

The main checkout is `root` (`resolveRoots().root`), outside `<root>/.tmp` and `<root>/.worktrees`. The gate (`gate-fat-tools.ts` `sharedCheckoutReason`, `worktree.ts` `mainCheckoutWriteReason` and `sharedGitReason`) answers for every caller, parent, scout and implementer alike, on every harness whose write tools it knows. It runs beside the `git worktree add` check, ahead of `reviewGuard` and every early return.

- Write: a write whose canonical target (after the scratch redirect) is in the main checkout is denied: `the main checkout is shared: run bun repo worktree add <name> and write under <root>/.worktrees/<name>; only <root>/.tmp/ is writable here`. A lesson Write is answered by orchestrate-parent before the gate, so it calls `mainCheckoutWriteReason` itself. `lessons.ts` `persistLesson`, `hitLesson` and `removeLesson` return `{ ok: false, error }` with the same text, and the CLI `hit`, `rm` and `index` exit 1; `match` and `check` stay read-only, and `writeIndex` is unguarded because `bun repo init` and `bun repo sync` call it in a consumer's main checkout.
- Git in the main checkout: `commit`, `merge`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`, `am` and `pull` are denied with `the main checkout is shared: commit inside <root>/.worktrees/<name>, then run cd <root> && bun repo worktree finish <name>`. `stash`, `reset`, `checkout`, `switch`, `restore`, `clean` and `rebase` are denied with `git <sub> in the main checkout can destroy other sessions' work: do it inside your worktree, or run it here only when the user's message asks for git <sub>`.
- Anywhere in the repo: a force push (`-f`, `--force`, `--force-with-lease`, `+ref`); `branch -d|-D|-f|-m|-M` of the default branch; `update-ref` of the default branch. The default branch is `origin/HEAD`, else `init.defaultBranch`, `main` or `master` when it exists locally, else the main checkout's current branch.
- Own worktree: inside the managed worktree the effective cwd is in (`cd` and `git -C` are followed), every other git command runs, `stash`, `reset --hard`, `checkout`, `rebase` and `commit --amend` included.
- Exception: `.repo/tmp/sessions/<sid>/git-asked.json` holds `{ "words": [...] }`, rewritten on every user prompt (an empty list clears it) by orchestrate-parent on Claude, Codex and Grok `UserPromptSubmit` and on Cursor's `beforeSubmitPrompt`, and read by the gate by sid. A named word lets that subcommand run for the turn. Bare words grant only `stash`, `commit` (so `/commit` grants it), `rebase` and `cherry-pick`; a force push needs `force push`, `force-push`, `push -f` or `push --force`; every other subcommand needs the literal `git <sub>`, since "main checkout", "clean up" and "merge to main" are everyday phrases. A negation ("don't stash") matches too, so the `AGENTS.md` line still applies. Claude and Codex children share the parent's sid and so its grant; Grok and Cursor children do not. Antigravity (1.5.3) writes no file: every tool call carries the user's message as top-level `lastUserInput`, and the gate feeds it through the same word rules. Only the main agent's calls carry it; an agy subagent's calls carry `lastUserInput: ""`, so a child gets no grant and a spawn prompt cannot grant one. Antigravity's gated tools are `write_file {Path, Content}`, `edit_file {Path, Target, Replacement}` and `run_command {CommandLine}`; `read_file {Path, StartLine, EndLine}` is not gated. Headless `cursor-agent -p` (v2026.11.05) never fires `beforeSubmitPrompt` either, so no prompt can grant a git subcommand there and the denies still apply; the Cursor IDE was not tested.
- Fail-open: not a git repo, a repo with no commit yet, and an error inside the check let the call through. A missing `sid` or an unwritable `git-asked.json` means no grant, so the deny stands. `finish`, `prune` and the `WorktreeRemove` hook run git from node, never the shell, so the git deny cannot block them.
- Not parsed: `bash -c '...'`, `$(...)` and `xargs git` hide a git command from the gate. An `rtk` or `env VAR=v` prefix and `cd <dir>` or `git -C <dir>` are parsed; a heredoc body is not a command.
- Shell-write gap: `sed -i`, `>`, `tee` and `rm` write the main checkout past the write deny, and so do the `rm` hints in `bun repo doctor`. The commit deny is the backstop: the change cannot be committed there without the user's message naming commit.
- `bun repo init` and `bun repo sync` rewrite tracked files from node, so run them inside a worktree. Run in the main checkout they leave it dirty, and only the user can commit that.
- Unmanaged linked worktrees outside `.worktrees` (T3 Code, Claude Desktop) are outside the root, so writes there pass, `finish` cannot land them, and `/commit` there only commits. They are not "own worktree" for the git rules.

`bun repo worktree add <name>` makes `<root>/.worktrees/<name>` on `wt/<name>` and prints the path. When the root has `bun.lock` it also runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` in the new worktree (output on stderr, sub-second on a warm cache; a failure prints one line naming the command and the path still prints), so tools that look up `<cwd>/node_modules/.bin`, such as pipeline, work there.

`bun repo worktree finish [<name>]` lands the branch. With no name it takes the worktree its cwd is in; from the root it exits 2 (`run finish inside .worktrees/<name> or pass its name`). It refuses a dirty worktree (any `git status --porcelain` line, untracked files included) and one mid-rebase, rebases `wt/<name>` onto the default branch inside the worktree, fast-forwards the default (`merge --ff-only` when the root has it checked out, else `fetch . wt/<name>:<default>`), then runs `git worktree remove` (never `--force`) and deletes the branch once the default holds it. If the default moved since the rebase, it rebases again, at most 3 tries (`<default> kept moving while finishing wt/<name>; run finish again`); a fast-forward that fails with the default unchanged reports git's reason with no retry (the root's own changes to the same file do this). A conflict aborts the rebase, keeps the worktree and names the files: resolve them in the worktree, rerun the checks, run `finish` again. A branch with no commits of its own is removed with `wt/<name> has no commits of its own; removed <path>`. Before it deletes a branch the default holds, `finish` (and `prune`) deletes origin's copy when `refs/remotes/origin/wt/<name>` exists, with `git push --no-verify origin --delete wt/<name>`, no prompt and a 30s limit; on failure it warns `could not delete origin's wt/<name>: <git's reason>; run git push origin --delete wt/<name>` and goes on. With origin's branch and tracking ref gone, the push gate no longer holds a Stop on the old run of `wt/<name>`. A rerun after a crash converges: a merged branch with no worktree is deleted, origin's copy first. When the root has the default branch checked out and can run `bun repo` (a `repo` script in its `package.json`, or a `repo` bin in `node_modules/.bin`), `finish` then runs `bun repo sync` there, output on stderr, so the root's generated configs match the new tree; on failure it warns `could not sync <root>: run bun repo sync there` and still exits 0. On success it prints `merged wt/<name> into <default> at <sha> and removed <path>; your shell may still be in it: cd <root>`. Run it from the root: `cd <root> && bun repo worktree finish <name>`. Run inside the worktree it removes, the work succeeds but Claude's Bash reports exit 1 (its own `pwd` fails in the deleted directory); check the `merged …` line and do not rerun.

`bun repo doctor` lists a managed worktree with commits the default lacks and a last commit 7 or more days old as `stale worktree <path> (wt/<name>, last commit <n> days ago)` with the `finish <name>` command. Younger ones are live work and are not listed.

`bun repo doctor` `agent models` checks that each model a generated agent names is still offered by its CLI: `.codex/agents/*.toml`, `.grok/agents/*.md`, `.grok/roles/*.toml` and `[subagents.models]` in `agents/global-settings/grok.toml`, `.agents/agents/*.md` (Antigravity) and `.cursor/agents/*.md`. Claude agents use the aliases `haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus` and are not checked. Cursor agents use `model: inherit` (the parent session's model, which any Cursor plan can run; a pinned Claude id is listed on a Free plan but refused), and `inherit` is not checked. Codex and agy are checked without running a command. Codex's list comes from `~/.codex/models_cache.json` `models[].slug` (a file). Agy's is a fixed set, the only values agy accepts for an agent's `model:`: `inherit`, `flash`, `pro` and `flash_lite`. `agy models` lists session models, which an agent file cannot name, and agy silently drops an agent whose `model:` is anything else. An agy main agent's `model:` is ignored (it runs on the session model), so the orchestrator uses `inherit`. An agy agent with no `tools:` gets a read-only default, so the orchestrator lists its tools. Grok's and Cursor's lists come from `grok models` and `cursor-agent --list-models`; those two commands run in parallel under one 20 s cap. A dropped model prints `<file>: model <id> is not offered by <cli>; offered: <ids>`. Grok or Cursor is skipped with its reason when it is not installed or its list fails or takes over 20 s, and codex when its cache is missing or malformed (`agent models  ok (skipped: ...)`). Agy is never skipped. Report only: the row never fails the run.

## Implementation format (SSOT)

Local session journal for `/implement-plan-deep`. Not a plan, handoff, or git commit.

Created when `/implement-plan-deep` starts. Straight shots skip this file. Do not merge into the plan (plan = flip the box only).

### Path

`.repo/implementations/{serial}-{slug}-{YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ}.md`

- **serial:** own counter (not plan serials). Unpadded decimal int ≥ 1. Never `0001`.
- **filename:** unpadded serial, slug, UTC datetime stamp. Same regex as new plans: `^[0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*-\d{8}T\d{6}Z\.md$`
- **lookup:** integer equality on leading digits.
- Frontmatter `serial:` line must match `^serial: [1-9][0-9]*$`.
- New writes always stamped. Collision: increment serial, same stamp.

### Link

Frontmatter `plan:` is the plan serial (`6`) or `none`. Own serial stays independent.

### Slugify / allocate

Same as plans (`slugify`, `nextSerial` on this dir). Body line 1: `IMPL_NAME: <3-6 word name>`. Optional `IMPL_PLAN: <n|none>` (default `none`).

### Frontmatter (required)

```yaml
---
serial: 1
plan: 6                 # unpadded int or none
name: add-auth
status: in-progress     # in-progress | done | blocked
created: 2026-08-26T14:30:00Z
source: "<≤120 chars of user task>"
---
```

#### Status machine

`in-progress` → `done` | `blocked`

- Fresh write: `in-progress`
- Plan Verify done and journal caught up: `done`
- Cannot finish: `blocked` (`## Blockers` must not be `(none)`)

### Body headings (this order only)

`# {slug}`, `## Done`, `## Issue`, `## Files`, `## Log`, `## Blockers`, `## Notes`

No other `##` headings.

| Section | Amount |
|---|---|
| Done | bullets. What landed and why. Past tense. Fresh: `(none)` |
| Issue | bug root cause bullets, or `(none)` |
| Files | repo-relative product paths as `- path` bullets. Default `/commit` stage set. No abs paths. No `.tmp/`. Fresh: `(none)` |
| Log | append-only. Fresh: `(none)`. After each plan leaf: `N.M [x] one line` (notes, fail, skip). `[x]` allowed |
| Blockers | open problems. `(none)` unless `status: blocked` |
| Notes | short leftovers, or `(none)` |

### Write

Write under `.repo/implementations/` (any filename in that dir). Grok `orchestrate-parent.ts` runs `cli/scripts/persist-implementation.ts` on create (`IMPL_NAME:`): serial/slug from the name, injects frontmatter, rewrites path + content. Updates to an existing file keep the path; full-body writes are validated in place. Invalid create/update denies — fix the body, do not retry elsewhere.

Host without that hook: name the file per **Path**, or pipe the body to `bun repo persist implementation --workspace {repo}` and use its `absPath`.

Never allocate a new serial to log a leaf. Append Log, update Files/Done, flip the plan box.

### Validation checklist

- filename stamped unpadded; serial int equals leading digits; `name` equals slug
- frontmatter keys: `serial`, `plan`, `name`, `status`, `created`, `source`
- `plan` is `none` or unpadded int ≥ 1; `status` ∈ `in-progress` | `done` | `blocked`
- headings in order only; no extra `##`
- Done / Issue / Files / Log / Blockers / Notes: bullets and/or `(none)`; none of those sections empty
- Files: repo-relative; reject abs and `.tmp/`
- `status: blocked` ⇒ Blockers is not only `(none)`

### Worked example

File: `.repo/implementations/1-notes-export-json-20260826T143000Z.md`

```markdown
---
serial: 1
plan: 1
name: notes-export-json
status: in-progress
created: 2026-08-26T14:30:00Z
source: "add --json to notes export"
---

# notes-export-json

## Done
- `notes export --json` prints every note as one JSON array; the text table stays the default

## Issue
(none)

## Files
- src/cli.ts
- src/export.ts
- src/export.test.ts

## Log
1.1 [x] read principle-test-behavior-not-implementation
2.1 [x] export tests for two notes and for none
2.2 [x] new cases fail on the unknown flag
3.1 [x] parse --json in cli.ts
3.2 [x] print JSON.stringify of the notes in export.ts
3.3 [x] export tests pass

## Blockers
(none)

## Notes
(none)
```

## Jev

Closed external decision. The source text is already saved. The question is a yes/no or a named choice. One call. Not open research. Not code. Not job.

### Availability

```
bun repo jev --available
```

Prints `yes` or `no` and exits 0. No request. No setup line.

`no`: the session answers the question itself. Do not run the decision command. Do not mention Jev, a missing key, or setup.

`yes`: continue below.

A key is `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or `apiKey` in `~/.workerstack/jev.json` (mode 0600). Env wins. Setup, when a person asks for it: `bun repo setup jev`. Spec: `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/setup.md`.

### Decision

Write `.repo/scratch/jev/<slug>-state.txt` (plain text or a JSON object) and `.repo/scratch/jev/<slug>-questions.json` (the System One questions map). Put every label for that study in the one map. At most 8 questions. State at most 64000 characters.

```
bun repo jev --state .repo/scratch/jev/<slug>-state.txt --questions .repo/scratch/jev/<slug>-questions.json
```

Yes/no:

```json
{ "keep": { "type": "noul", "instructions": "Does this passage promise zero retention on the default plan?" } }
```

Named choice:

```json
{
  "endpoint": {
    "type": "choice",
    "instructions": "Which endpoint should the app call?",
    "criteria": {
      "typesafe": "Vendor host, path, and key",
      "other": "A different host, path, or key"
    }
  }
}
```

Model is `jev-1.13.0`. Stdout is at most 8 lines: model, input tokens, then one label line. Exit 0. Use that label and confidence. A low confidence is the result. Do not rephrase and call again.

One request per process. UTC-day ledger `~/.workerstack/jev-usage.json` stops at 40 requests or 1000000 input tokens. A 429 or 529 retries once only when `Retry-After` is at most 2 seconds.

Exit 2 means the decision call did not return a label. Answer from the sources. Do not invent a label. Do not print the key or the state.

## Lessons

Mistakes that outlive one task. One committed file per mistake under `.repo/lessons/`, with a generated index. Not host memory: everything is in the repo and reaches every machine through git.

### Three layers

- **Plan:** `## Previous mistakes` in each plan holds that task's details: rejected approaches, failed Verify, accepted review findings. It stays with the plan in `.tmp/`. Format: `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/plan-format.md`.
- **Roadmap:** `## Previous mistakes` in a roadmap holds mistakes about the program: slice order, slice boundaries, and `slice` entries for what a child plan found that changed later slices. A roadmap saved in the old shape also logs its Decisions there; a pointer roadmap's decisions live in the slice plans. It lasts as long as the program, in `.tmp/`. Format: `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/roadmap-format.md`.
- **Repo:** a lesson holds a mistake our normal workflow will hit again on other tasks. A one-time issue stays in the plan's Previous mistakes. A plan entry that generalizes becomes a lesson, and the entry ends with `(lesson: {slug})`.

### File

`.repo/lessons/{slug}.md`: a title (the rule, at most 72 chars), `## Mistake` (at most 280) and `## Fix` (at most 360), with nothing between the title and `## Mistake`. Every save, `bun repo lessons check` and `bun repo sync --check` refuse a lesson over a cap or with a line under the title.

```markdown
---
name: plan-forks
paths: ["cli/scripts/persist-plan.ts", "agents/grok/hooks/**"]
hits: 1
last-hit: 2026-11-01
evidence: ["plan 16"]
---

# Plan rewrites fork serials

## Mistake
What went wrong, concretely.

## Fix
What to do instead.
```

- `name` is the filename slug. `paths` are repo-relative globs (`**` spans dirs; `*` and `?` stay in one segment) and each must match a file that exists.
- `hits` counts occurrences. `evidence` keeps the 5 most recent plan serials or commits.
- A new lesson may leave out `hits` and `last-hit`; the save fills `1` and today.

### Index

`.repo/lessons/INDEX.md` is generated: one line per lesson (`- \`slug\` (hits N): title`), sorted by hits. It opens with the `@generated by @workerstack/repo` header and is left read-only (0444); to change it, edit the lessons in `.repo/lessons/`. Every lesson save, `hit`, and `rm` rewrites it, and `bun repo sync` rewrites it too. `bun repo sync --check` fails on index drift, an invalid lesson, or a glob that matches no file.

### Write

- Write, `hit`, `rm` and `index` run inside a worktree: the plan's `{serial}-{name}` (`bun repo worktree add {serial}-{name}` if it is missing), else `lesson-{slug}`, and `/correct` uses its `correct-{slug}`. The lesson then lands with that worktree's commit and `finish` (run from the root). In the main checkout the Write is denied, `hit`, `rm` and `index` exit 1 with `the main checkout is shared: run bun repo worktree add <name> and write under <root>/.worktrees/<name>; only <root>/.tmp/ is writable here`, and the library calls return `{ ok: false, error }` with that text.
- Write the whole file. The hook validates it, renders the standard form, and reindexes; the host saves it. An Edit of a lesson is denied.
- `bun repo lessons hit <slug> --evidence <text>` counts a repeat. The same evidence counts once.
- `bun repo lessons rm <slug>` deletes a lesson and reindexes.
- `bun repo lessons index` rebuilds the index. `check` runs the checks and, like `match`, is read-only, so it runs anywhere.

### When to write

Write a lesson only for a mistake our normal workflow will hit again on other tasks. A one-time issue stays in the plan's Previous mistakes.

After any of these, add a `## Previous mistakes` entry to the plan. If the mistake will happen again on other tasks, run `bun repo lessons match` on the files involved first, then `hit` the matching lesson or write a new one.

- Plan feedback from the user (`/write-plan-deep`).
- A failed Verify, or a test that failed after a fix (`/implement-plan-deep`).
- `principle-attack-the-premise` firing (`/implement-plan-deep`).
- An accepted `/review-plan` finding (`/write-plan-deep`).
- Roadmap feedback, an accepted `/review-roadmap` finding (`/write-roadmap-deep`), a child plan that changes the program, or a failed program Verify (`/implement-roadmap-deep`). These go to the roadmap's log. Before the roadmap is `done`, each entry that outlives the program becomes a lesson with `--evidence "roadmap {n}"`.
- An operator correction (`/correct`).

At `hits: 2` the mistake is a class. `/correct` encodes it as a check (architecture, type, lint, or test), then runs `bun repo lessons rm`.

### When to read

- `bun repo lessons match <file...>` prints the lessons whose globs match, most hits first, 10 at most. It reads the lesson files, not `INDEX.md`; a lesson it cannot read is named on stderr (`.repo/lessons/x.md: invalid, run bun repo lessons check`) and skipped. Each file is matched against the lessons of the checkout that holds it: the root or a managed worktree; a file in an unmanaged linked worktree uses the checkout you run it from.
- A new plan that names a matched file must cite that lesson's path in Watch-outs, or the save is denied with the lesson listed.
- The first time a session edits a matched file, the hook adds that lesson's title and path to the context. Each lesson is shown once per session.
- `/review-plan` reads the matched lessons and flags one that no leaf acts on.

## Listen

Speech-to-text from the session. Input only. Not TTS. Not a live voice agent. Not MCP.

```
bun repo listen whoami
bun repo listen devices
bun repo listen rec [--seconds 8] [--device D] [--clip]
bun repo listen start [--device D]
bun repo listen stop [--clip]
bun repo listen toggle [--clip]
bun repo listen status
bun repo listen file --path clip.wav [--clip]
bun repo listen latest
```

`rec` records then transcribes (default 8s, cap 120s). `toggle` is the hotkey verb: first run starts, second run stops and prints the transcript. Audio and `latest.txt` live under `.repo/tmp/listen/`. `--cwd /path/to/repo` when the hotkey does not already run in the repo.

### Auth and capture

Handheld (any OS): `bun repo setup listen` or `bun repo setup` → listen. Prints OS install commands for ffmpeg / whisper-cli (does not run them), optional ggml download into `~/.workerstack/whisper/`, OpenAI fallback key if local STT is missing.

If ffmpeg, whisper-cli, a ggml model, or `OPENAI_API_KEY` is missing, the CLI prints `setup: bun repo setup listen` and exits 1. Agents should show that line, not a stack or JSON. Do not invent a key.

STT prefers **local whisper.cpp**. Install the binary; the first `listen` downloads `ggml-base.en.bin` (~142MB) into `~/.workerstack/whisper/`. No API cost after that. If the binary or download is missing, it falls back to OpenAI `whisper-1` (`OPENAI_API_KEY` or `~/.workerstack/speak.json`). Force with `LISTEN_STT=local` or `LISTEN_STT=openai`. Never commit keys.

| | env | `~/.workerstack/speak.json` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local model | `WHISPER_MODEL` | `listen.whisperModel` |
| Force engine | `LISTEN_STT` | `listen.stt` (`auto` / `local` / `openai`) |
| OpenAI key | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `openai.apiKey` |
| OpenAI model | `LISTEN_MODEL` | `listen.model` (default `whisper-1`) |
| Device | `LISTEN_DEVICE` | `listen.device` |
| Seconds | `LISTEN_SECONDS` | `listen.seconds` |

#### Local Whisper (preferred)

One install:

- mac: `brew install whisper-cpp` (provides `whisper-cli`)
- linux: build https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp (`whisper-cli` on PATH)
- win: whisper.cpp release `whisper-cli.exe` on PATH

Then `bun repo listen whoami` or `rec`. The first run fetches `ggml-base.en.bin` to `~/.workerstack/whisper/`. Do not pip-install OpenAI Whisper. Do not curl the model yourself unless the auto-download fails.

Larger models: put another `ggml-*.bin` in that folder or set `WHISPER_MODEL`. Doctor reports `whisper-cli` as optional. `whoami` prints `stt=local` or `stt=openai`.

#### ffmpeg (mic only)

- mac: `brew install ffmpeg`
- linux: `sudo apt install ffmpeg`
- win: `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg`

`file` and `latest` work without a mic. Doctor reports ffmpeg as optional.

`rec` detaches ffmpeg and does not attach it to the IDE TTY. AVFoundation can stall forever on a VS Code / Electron PTY even when Visual Studio Code already has Microphone access.

Default devices: mac `:0` (AVFoundation audio 0), linux Pulse `default` (ALSA if the id is `hw:…`), Windows requires `--device` or `LISTEN_DEVICE` from `listen devices`.

### Hotkeys

Bind one key to toggle. Include `--clip` so the transcript is on the clipboard as well as `latest.txt`.

```
bun --cwd /ABS/repo repo listen toggle --clip
```

Replace `/ABS/repo` with the repo root.

- **mac:** Shortcuts (Run Shell Script) or skhd: `hyper - r : bun --cwd /ABS/repo repo listen toggle --clip`
- **win:** PowerToys Keyboard Manager or AutoHotkey: `^!r:: Run, bun --cwd C:\ABS\repo repo listen toggle --clip, C:\ABS\repo, Hide`
- **linux:** desktop custom shortcut or sxhkd to the same command.

No daemon. Each keypress is one CLI. First press records; second press transcribes.

`--clip` uses `pbcopy` (mac), `clip` (win), or `wl-copy` / `xclip` / `xsel` (linux).

## Map

Cheap outline. Not a file dump.

### Protocol
- `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/cascade.md` — session agent tools; job first; spawn scout when the dump needs judgment
- `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/rtk.md` — shell compression
- `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/browser.md` — Lightpanda-first session CLI (`nav|snap|click|fill|scroll|wait|hover|select|shot|pdf|stop`); not MCP
- `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/hooks.md` — hook policy
- `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/map.md` — this file
- `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/output.md` — default voice
- `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/scope.md` — size gate; plan by default: research → `/write-plan-deep` → approval → `/implement-plan-deep`; two or more slices → `/write-roadmap-deep`
- `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/INDEX.md` — the catalog, read first: the generated `repo:refs` (one line per reference doc), `repo:stack` (the stack's installed packages) and `repo:available` (the published ones not installed) sections. INDEX always. Not if-maps-else

### Agent SSOT
- Docs SoT: `agents/skills` + `references/` (shipped in the package; a consumer reads `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/`). `bun repo sync` maps anything placed there. `.claude/skills/<name>` and `.agents/skills/<name>` are generated links to `agents/skills/<name>`, not SoT; no mirror scan
- The trees come from `cli/sync/agents/` (`sources` `frontmatter` `rules` `subagents` `hooks`) via `bun repo sync`, reading the stock sources in `agents/` (exported as `@workerstack/repo/agents/*`)
- `agents/subagents/{orchestrator,repo}.md`
- `agents/rules/overview.md` → `AGENTS.md`
- A consumer's own content lives in `.repo/` (below) and `references/`; both are committed, and `bun repo sync` merges them over the package's
- Default output: `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/output.md` (overview.md → AGENTS.md; also agent bodies, not auto-injected)

### Skills layout
- Source: `agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, the one copy (`STOCK_SKILLS_REL` in `cli/scripts/skill-conflicts.ts`) in this repo. A consumer's own skills go to `.repo/skills/<name>/`, and one named like a stock skill replaces it
- A consumer's `bun repo sync` links each stock skill (and each `.repo/skills/<name>`) into `.agents/skills/<name>` for codex and antigravity and into `.claude/skills/<name>` for claude, as a directory symlink (a junction with an absolute target on Windows): to the generated `.agents/skills/<name>` when there is one, else straight to the skill. Optional packs (`google-workspace` `listen` `speak` `clasp`) are linked only when `agents.skills` names them, and a config pack can gate a stock skill the same way (the `benchmark` pack links `/benchmark`). In this repo sync links both `.claude/skills/<name>` and `.agents/skills/<name>` straight to `agents/skills/<name>` with a relative link. The package ships no generated trees, so each consumer's sync makes its links
- Read directly: Codex and Antigravity read `.agents/skills`; Grok reads `.grok/skills`, `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills` (deduplicated by name); Cursor reads `.cursor/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.codex/skills`, `.grok/skills` and `.agents/skills` (follows symlinks, deduplicates by realpath)
- There is no skills generator step: `bun repo sync` only links skills; nothing wipes `.agents/skills`

### Grok hand files
- `cli/scripts/orchestrate-parent.ts` + `agents/grok/hooks/orchestrate-parent.json` — spawn/fat/stop/persist / SubagentStop intercept / session receipt
- `bun repo sync` prunes what it wrote last run and no longer plans (the `.repo/tmp/sync.json` manifest); a path outside the manifest is never removed
- `agents/grok/hooks/rtk.json` — RTK
- `agents/global-settings/` — `manifest.json` (hosts `claude` `codex` `grok` `antigravity` `cursor` `opencode`: `format`, `payload`, `dest` under `$HOME`) and one payload per host (`claude.json` `codex.toml` `grok.toml` `antigravity.json` `cursor.json` `opencode.json`); `sync-global-settings.ts` (`bun repo yolo`) merges each into its dest (not auto-loaded; project `.grok/config.toml` cannot set `[features]`)
- `agents/mcp-policy.jsonc` — MCP deny-default SSOT (`default: deny`, `allow: []`)
- `agents/grok/{roles,hooks}/` — grok's static roles and hook configs; `bun repo sync` copies them into `.grok/roles` and `.grok/hooks`
- `agents/skills/<name>/` — the one skills source; `bun repo sync` links each into the host skill dirs

- `cli/scripts/check-globals.ts` — every manifest payload key (minus `skipKeyPattern`) must be present in its `$HOME` dest; project `.grok/config.toml` sets no `[features]` or `[agent]`. Not in `bun repo sync --check`: `bun cli/scripts/check-globals.ts` in this repo and the `bun repo doctor` `globals` row everywhere

- `cli/scripts/parse-need.ts`
- `cli/scripts/persist-handoff.ts` — `.repo/handoffs/{serial}-{slug}-{stamp}.md`

- `cli/scripts/purge-global-mcps.ts`
- `cli/scripts/emit-mcp-policy.ts`
- `cli/scripts/emit-agent-shell-tools.ts`
- `cli/scripts/browser.ts` — session browser rail
- `cli/scripts/google-workspace.ts` — Sheets Docs Slides Calendar Gmail Drive
- `cli/scripts/speak.ts` — TTS
- `cli/scripts/listen.ts` — STT
- `cli/scripts/setup.ts` — handheld speak / listen / google-workspace / browser (`~/.workerstack/`)
- `cli/scripts/doctor.ts` — unified prereqs; `globals` row (ok or first drift line); optional google-workspace (`oauth` `tokens` `adc` `clasprc`), speak, clasp, ffmpeg, whisper-cli
- `cli/env/` — the `@workerstack/repo/env` module (`index` exports; `define` merge and views; `keys` identities and the keys file; `age` encrypt and decrypt); `cli/env.ts` holds `defineEnv` and `sealed`, which decrypt in a bun child
- `cli/repo-env.ts` — this repo's own env (`repoEnv`): its process variables; add a name there to read one

- `cli/scripts/env-files.ts` — finds the `defineEnv` files, picks one (`--file`, the one declaring the key, the only one) and lists USED BY
