- `cli/scripts/env-keys.ts` — `env init`, `key import`, `key ci`: the key pair, the keys file and the `gh secret set`
- `cli/scripts/env-values.ts` — `env ls`, `get`, `run`, `export`: masked reads, the child env and dotenv quoting
- `cli/__fixtures__/env-repo.ts` — builds a scratch git repo with a keys file and an env file for the `env-*.test.ts` files
- `cli/check-env-values.ts` (+ `.constants.ts`) — the three `bun repo check` env rules over every file that calls `defineEnv(`: plain secret, key one scope lacks, undeclared process read
- `cli/check-deps.ts` (+ `.constants.ts`) — the `bun repo check` deps rule per public package: a used dep outside `peerDependencies`, any dep of a library (no `bin`), missing export types, an unreadable surface
- `cli/type-surface.ts` (+ `.constants.ts`) — the in-memory declaration emit of a package's typed exports over a virtual host, and the packages its declarations use, keyed to the export that reaches each file
- `cli/type-surface-entries.ts` — the files the types of `exports` start from: exact keys, `*` patterns, `null` exclusions, tsconfig `files`, the `types`/`typings`/`main` fallback, and the keys whose types are missing
- `cli/type-surface-scan.ts` — the bare imports, `/// <reference types>` and globals of the emitted declarations, each charged to the package that declares it, and the own files each imports
- `cli/type-surface-blame.ts` — reads a JSON or JSONC file's fields, and charges a used package declared in no field to the deps one hop up
- `cli/build-outputs.ts` — maps each `tsconfig.build.json` output to its source; none for a missing or unparsable config
- `cli/packed-under.ts` — the files under a dir and whether npm packs each, by `files` (globs, dirs, `!` negations) or the default skips
- `cli/package-locator.ts` — the package that owns a file: the nearest named `package.json`, memoized
- `cli/__fixtures__/deps-kit.ts`, `cli/__fixtures__/surface-kit.ts` — scratch package trees for the `check-deps` and `type-surface*` tests

### Tmp
- `.repo/plans/` — persist-plan; format SSOT = `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/plan-format.md`
- `.repo/implementations/` — persist-implementation; format SSOT = `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/implementation-format.md`
- `.repo/tmp/orchestrator-logs/` — need-intercept, session-gate, stop-block stamps
- `.repo/scratch/` — scratch + `/tmp` dumps `{serial}-{slug}-{stamp}.{ext}` at root (not nested `tmp/`)
- `.repo/tmp/browser/` — browser session/profile/shot/pdf (not MCP)
- `.repo/handoffs/` — persist-handoff / `/handoff`
- `.repo/tmp/stash/` — job / snap overflow
- `.repo/tmp/sessions/{sid}/` — wrote/read/receipt
- `.repo/tmp/speak/` — TTS mp3
- `.repo/tmp/listen/` — STT wav + `latest.txt`

### `.repo/` layout
Repo-owned content, committed. In this repo `.repo/` holds `lessons/` and the ignored `tmp/`.
- `lessons/` — one file per lesson plus the generated `INDEX.md`
- `rules/` — path-scoped rules only (each has `paths`), written to the host rule trees; a rule without `paths` is moved by one sync below the `repo:rules` region of its scope's `AGENTS.md` (except one with `overrides`); a stock rule's extra sections go to `<name>-local.md` so the stock text stays live
- `subagents/` — extra agents; one named like a stock agent replaces it
- `skills/` — extra skills, linked into each host tree (a real skill dir found under `.agents/skills` or `.claude/skills` moves here)
- `settings/claude.json` — keys deep-merged into the generated `.claude/settings.json`
- `hooks.jsonc` — replaces the stock hooks whole
- `mcp-policy.jsonc` — deep-merged over the stock MCP policy
- `permissions.json` — path deny rules added to the generated hooks
- `lint-baseline.json` — per file, per rule, the lint problems still allowed; read by `bun repo turn` and `bun repo check`
- `test-times.json` — whole milliseconds per test file, written by `bun repo ci times`; read by the vitest shard sequencer
- `global-settings/` — a payload of the stock's name here (`claude.json`, `codex.toml`, `grok.toml`, `antigravity.json`, `cursor.json`, `opencode.json`) replaces that stock payload whole in `bun repo yolo` and the `globals` check; the stock manifest stays
- `bench/` — `<name>.bench.ts` specs, a `defineBench` default export each; read by `bun repo bench <name>`, not by sync; root only
- `env.keys.json` — `{ "recipient": "age1…", "repo": "<name>" }`: the age public key `sealed(...)` values are sealed for, and the name of the key file `~/.workerstack/keys/<repo>.key`
- `tmp/` — ignored: `sync.json` (the manifest) and `stage/` (the build dir, removed after each sync)

### Generated (do not hand-edit)
`bun repo sync` writes these from `node_modules/@workerstack/repo` plus `.repo/` for the hosts in `agents.hosts` (default: all five; `HOST_TREES` in `cli/sync/hosts.ts` is the one table). In a consumer they are gitignored and recreated by every `bun install`; in this repo they are committed. `bun repo sync --check` reports drift. Three more `agents` keys in `repo.config.ts`: `defaultStrategy` (`free`, `spawn-fast` or `spawn-deep`; default `free`) is the `strategy:` a new plan or roadmap gets when saved without one, read by the plan save; `defaultMode` (`ask` or `away`; default `ask`) applies when the session has no `/ask` or `/away` stamp and no in-progress plan or roadmap with a `mode:`, read by the session gate; `defaultEffort` (`fast` or `deep`; default `deep`) picks the skill pair the last line of the root `AGENTS.md` rules (and `CLAUDE.md` for claude) names, `/write-plan-fast` and `/implement-plan-fast` or the `-deep` pair, read by sync. Example: `agents: { defaultStrategy: "spawn-deep", defaultMode: "away", defaultEffort: "fast" }`. Each file sync writes whole opens with a `@generated by @workerstack/repo` header line where its format takes a comment and is left read-only (0444, 0555 for a hook) by every sync; to change one, edit its source in `.repo/` (the layout above) or in the package, then sync. A tracked file with that header that no output names any more is removed, even with no manifest; one under a `__fixtures__` folder is kept, and changing the header line keeps a copy. Files where sync owns only regions (`.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `references/INDEX.md`) stay writable. A region opens with `# repo:<name> <hash>` and closes with `# /repo:<name>` (`<!-- repo:<name> <hash> -->` and `<!-- /repo:<name> -->` in markdown); the hash is the first 8 hex of the sha256 of the body sync wrote. Sync never fails on a shared file: it prints one `<path>: <repair>` line on stderr per repair (`converted the old markers to repo:ignore` for the old `# >>> @workerstack/repo` pair, `added the hash to`, `closed`, `opened`, `reordered the markers of`, `rewrote the markers of`, `dropped 1 extra`, `dropped 1 stray marker of`, `moved 1 edited line out of` (kept just below the region), `cut` for a region no version writes any more). A shared path no output names any more has its regions cut and keeps the rest (`--check`: `<path> has regions no output writes`), removed only when nothing but whitespace is left. An invalid or non-object `.vscode/settings.json` is left as is with a warning. `bun repo sync` and `--check` refuse when git tracks a file the `repo:ignore` block of `.gitignore` covers, and print the `git rm --cached` command to run.
- `AGENTS.md` (the root and each package's) — shared: sync writes only the hashed `repo:rules` region at the top; everything else is your text, tracked and committed. There is no package `CLAUDE.md`. The always-on text over 12 KiB is a warning
- Not written by sync: `.mcp.json` is your tracked file (`bun repo init` writes the first one; sync never writes or deletes it). Every other host's MCP file is built from it, filtered by the MCP policy allow list; a `.repo/mcp.json` or a policy `servers` key is moved into `.mcp.json` by one sync, and `.mcp.json`'s own server wins on a name collision
- claude → `.claude/`: `agents/*`, `settings.json` (MCP keys, hooks, the `.repo/settings/claude.json` merge), `skills/<name>` links
- codex → `.codex/` (`agents/*`, `config.toml` `mcp_servers`, absent when allow empty) and `.agents/skills/<name>` links
- antigravity → `.agents/`: `agents/*`, `skills/<name>` links, `mcp_config.json`, hooks
- grok → `.grok/`: `agents/*`, `config.toml` (project MCP `[[permissions]]` + `[plugins] deny_default`; no `[features]`), `roles/scout.toml` and `hooks/*.json` copied from `agents/grok/`; the hook scripts stay in the package's `cli/scripts/`
- cursor → `.cursor/`: `hooks.json` (hooks-union adds consumer extras), `agents/scout.md`; a real dir, not shipped in the package
- release pack: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (tracked, whole-file; the e2e job only when the root has a `test:e2e` script, the `consumer` job only for a named public root); also, for a public root with a config `owner` and a GitHub `repository`, `SECURITY.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` and `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/{bug_report,config}.yml` (tracked, whole-file); a hand-written one is refused
- benchmark pack: `.github/workflows/bench.yml` (tracked, whole-file), which `bun repo bench --remote` dispatches with the spec, the OSes and the sha; a hand-written one is refused; also the `/benchmark` skill links in `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills`
- evals pack: `.github/workflows/eval.yml` (tracked, whole-file), dispatched by hand with an eval name and a cost cap, and the evals environment `bun repo github` manages; a hand-written eval.yml is refused
- standards pack, editor: keys the file lacks are added to `.vscode/settings.json`, and ids it lacks to `recommendations` in `.vscode/extensions.json`, never changing what you set: Bun formats on save through the Simple LSP Client extension (`bun fmt --no-script --stdin-filepath`), the oxc extension only lints (`oxc.enable.oxfmt: false`, fix-all on save), the workspace TypeScript (`js/ts.tsdk.path`, with the TypeScript 7 extension for 7 or later; a deprecated `typescript.tsdk` moves to `js/ts.tsdk.path`), `.css` as `tailwindcss` with a Tailwind entry sheet, the Vitest extension when vitest is installed
- always: `bunfig.toml`, the `repo:ignore` region of `.gitignore`, the `repo:generated` region of `.gitattributes`, `references/INDEX.md` regions `repo:refs`, `repo:packages`, `repo:stack` and `repo:available`, `.repo/lessons/INDEX.md` when lessons exist, `.vscode/tasks.json` (committed in a consumer too)

### Generator divergences
Where `cli/sync/agents/` differs from the rulesync 43.7.0 it replaced:
- YAML 1.2 parsing: `yes` stays a string
- No 80-column folding of long values
- The `agentsmd` and `codexcli` rule targets both fold into `AGENTS.md` only
- A leading `./` in a claude hook command becomes `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/`
- A bad subagent, or a rule without frontmatter, fails sync

## Output

en-US default. Detail behind the reply rules in `overview.md`, which stays the source for voice and shape.

Cue names are examples too: example, e.g., for instance, such as, and so on, `…`, `etc.`, a sketched sentence, or one labeled case. Do not reuse one reply for every turn. Pick the count and the form for this case.

A closed instruction stays literal. Cues of that kind include only, exactly, just these, verbatim, no others, a schema, an identifier, a command, or quoted text. When an open cue and a closed cue both apply, the closed cue wins.

Do not invent a question or let the close introduce new numbers. Completed work uses past verbs and paths. If more work remains, say what. Ask in English when a choice is real.

`/su`, `/bro`, `/unslop`, `/blast-radius`, `/correct`, `/teach`, plan files, commit subjects, and job stdout keep their own shape. `/bro` restates a reply that missed the voice in `overview.md`. `/explain` keeps the shape and may lengthen the middle. Repo children do not talk to the user.

Job stdout is a sentence plus up to 6 dash facts, cap 8 lines, and an optional `stash=` receipt.

### Example: waiting on the user

One case of the class "the user must act before we can finish". Copy the shape, not the words.

Cold:

> We're waiting on four things, and only the first is mine to do now.
>
> 1. Local main isn't pushed. It's 10 commits ahead of origin, including my test fix. Nothing below can start until those commits reach origin.
> 2. The first public-sync run after that push. It should copy the generated code into each public repo.
> 3. Publish secrets. None of the public repos I checked has its own secrets or variables. They may be set at the org level, but my token can't read org settings.
> 4. Your go to publish.
>
> Should I push main myself, or keep waiting?

Partner:

> We're one push away from the first releases, and most of what's left is yours.
>
> **You**
> - Push main, or tell me to. It's 10 commits ahead, including another session's work.
> - NuGet (`org/sdk-csharp`): add a trusted publishing policy for `release.yml`, and the repo variable `NUGET_USER`.
> - Maven (`org/sdk-java`): add the user token as `MAVEN_CENTRAL_USERNAME` and `MAVEN_CENTRAL_PASSWORD`, and the GPG key as `MAVEN_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` plus `MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE`. Skip any already set at the org level; my token can't see org settings.
>
> **Me**: writing the test that blocks a release when the spec differs from prod, now. After the push I run the public sync, cut the releases, and verify each registry on Linux, macOS and Windows.
>
> Say "publish" when the secrets are in.

The partner reply opens on the goal, groups the user's steps by where they do them, says what the agent does next, and ends on one action.

## Plan format (SSOT)

Local session checklist. Not a design doc, PR stack, or DAG.

### Path

`.repo/plans/{serial}-{slug}-{YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ}.md`

- **serial:** unpadded decimal int only (`1`, `12`, `10000`). **Never** `0001`, never quoted `"0001"` / `"1"`. Serial ≥ 1.
- **filename:** unpadded serial, slug, UTC datetime stamp (`6-sync-global-settings-20260826T143000Z.md`, not `0001-slug.md`). Stamp is `created` with `-` and `:` dropped (keep `T` and `Z`).
- **lookup:** integer equality on leading digits (`1` matches `1-foo-20260826T143000Z.md` and legacy `1-foo.md`; also `0001-foo.md` if an old padded file still exists).
- **valid filename (new):** `^[0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*-\d{8}T\d{6}Z\.md$`
- **valid filename (legacy):** `^[0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*\.md$` (no stamp; still accepted for existing files)
- Frontmatter line must match `^serial: [1-9][0-9]*$`. Leading zeros are invalid (YAML octal / VS Code warning).
- **New writes** always use the stamped filename. Collision: increment serial, rebuild filename, same stamp.

### Slugify (`PLAN_NAME`)

Send `PLAN_NAME: <name>` as the body's first line. The save reads the name from it and drops the line wherever it sits above the first `##` outside a code fence, so a body that opens with `commit:` or `strategy:` lines still saves with the card right under the title. A `PLAN_NAME:` line inside a fence or below the first `##` stays as text.

1. lower
2. non `[a-z0-9]` → `-`
3. collapse `-`, strip edges
4. trim to 50 chars; if cut on `-`, strip trailing `-`
5. empty → `unnamed`
6. strip trailing `.lock` if any

### Allocate next serial (repo, bash)

```bash
mkdir -p .repo/plans
next=1
for f in .repo/plans/*; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  b=$(basename "$f")
  case "$b" in
    [0-9]*.md) n=${b%%-*}; n=$((10#$n)); [ "$n" -ge "$next" ] && next=$((n+1));;
  esac
done
# filename prefix: unpadded decimal "$next" (1, 12, 10000)
```

Collision: if target path exists, increment and retry (max 5).

### Frontmatter (required)

```yaml
---
serial: 1
name: add-auth
status: ready          # ready | in-progress | done | blocked
reviews: 0             # settled /review-plan rounds; never lowered or removed
created: 2026-08-26T14:30:00Z    # UTC ISO-8601 seconds + Z; no milliseconds
source: "<≤120 chars of user task>"
commit: feat: <subject>
strategy: free          # free | spawn-fast | spawn-deep
mode: away             # optional: ask | auto | away
---
```

`name` is the slug only (no datetime). `source` ≤120 chars.

`strategy` is optional. Omit it to take `agents.defaultStrategy`, else `free`. It says how the plan gets implemented:

- `free`: the main session works as it would in a plain chat; it may spawn agents but nothing forces it to.
- `spawn-fast`: the main session only reviews. Each phase goes to the `implementer-fast` agent. The reviewer reads the real diff, reruns the tests and sends findings back. A second attempt goes to `implementer-deep`.
- `spawn-deep`: the same loop, with `implementer-deep` from the first attempt.

A save with no `strategy` gets `agents.defaultStrategy`, else `free`. An unknown value is denied with `strategy: free|spawn-fast|spawn-deep`. A body line `strategy: {value}` moves into the frontmatter after `commit:`, like `commit:`. A line inside a code fence is not moved. The person can change the value with a code such as `isf` when approving, or `hsf` when handing off.

`mode` is optional: `ask` or `away`. While the plan is `in-progress`, its `mode` applies only when the session has no `/ask` or `/away` stamp, for the session that saved it only. The order is the session stamp, then the in-progress `mode`, then `agents.defaultMode`, then `ask`. `/write-plan-deep` writes it only when the session runs `/away` or the person asked for a mode. A body line `mode: {value}` moves into the frontmatter after `strategy:`, like `strategy:`; a line inside a code fence is not moved. Another value is denied with `mode: ask|away`.

`reviews` counts the `/review-plan` rounds whose findings the writer settled: a whole number with no sign or leading zero, `0` on a new plan. The writer bumps it in the same save that applies a round's findings, even a round with no findings. It never goes down, and once present it cannot be removed, so every Write that sends full frontmatter carries the current `reviews`. The count proves a round ran and was settled, not that the review was good.

`created` for **new writes:** `new Date().toISOString()` with milliseconds stripped (`.\d{3}Z` → `Z`), e.g. `2026-08-26T14:30:00Z`. Existing files may still have `created: YYYY-MM-DD`.

#### Status machine

`ready` → `in-progress` → `done` | `blocked`

- Fresh write: `ready`
- Implement start: `in-progress`, only with `reviews` ≥ 1. The save denies the move with `reviews: 0`, and a missing `reviews` counts as 0. A plan already `in-progress` without the key stays editable
- All boxes `[x]`: `done`
- Cannot finish: `blocked` (leave remaining `[ ]`)

### Body headings (this order only)

`# {slug}`, the card, `## Goal`, `## Usage`, `## Context`, `## Constraints`, `## Watch-outs`, `## Steps`, `## Verify`, `## Previous mistakes`

No other `##` headings. A plan saved before `## Usage` or `## Previous mistakes` existed stays valid without them; a fresh save needs both. Lines inside a code fence are never headings or checkboxes. No PR Plan, Key Decisions, or DAG.
No required Why heading. Optional why footnote only (not a `##`). Pick2 file plan stays how-first; missing Why heading does not block.

### Card

The 5 lines a person reads first: right after `# {slug}` and one blank line, then a blank line before `## Goal`.

```markdown
WHAT   notes export --json prints a JSON array
WHY    scripts parse notes without the table
RISK   empty notebook must print []
TOUCH  src/cli.ts, src/export.ts (+ test)
DONE   bun run test; --json | JSON.parse ok
```

- Labels `WHAT`, `WHY`, `RISK`, `TOUCH`, `DONE`, in that order, each padded to 7 columns so the text starts at column 8. The text is never empty.
- Each line is at most 120 characters.
- The card sums up Goal and Steps for a person reviewing at a glance. It does not replace `## Goal`, which tools and `/review-plan` read.
- Fresh writes only. An update to a plan saved without a card stays valid.
- Each failing line has its own deny: `start with the 5-line card after the title: WHAT, WHY, RISK, TOUCH, DONE`, `card line 2 must start with WHY`, `card line 4 (TOUCH) is 131 characters; the limit is 120`.

### Size

At most 100 lines above `## Previous mistakes`, frontmatter included. More than that is two or more slices: write a roadmap with `/write-roadmap-deep`. A fresh save over the cap is denied with `131 lines above ## Previous mistakes, the cap is 100; split it into a roadmap (/write-roadmap-deep)`. An update over 100 lines is denied only when it is longer than the saved file, so a legacy plan can still flip boxes. `## Previous mistakes` never counts: it grows during the run.

### Previous mistakes

This plan's own log of what went wrong. Last heading, after Verify, no checkboxes. A new plan writes `(none)`.

- Entry: `- {source}: {what was wrong} → {what changed}`, optionally ending ` (lesson: {slug})`.
- `source`: `feedback` (the user sent the plan back), `verify` (a Verify or test failed after a fix), `review` (an accepted `/review-plan` finding), `premise` (an assumption turned out wrong), `decision` (a choice made under away instead of asking).
- A decision entry is `- decision: {question} → {choice}, because {why}`.
- Append-only. A save that edits or drops an existing entry is denied and names the entry.
- Write a lesson only for a mistake our normal workflow will hit again on other tasks. A one-time issue stays in the plan's Previous mistakes. An entry that will happen again on other tasks also becomes a lesson: `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/lessons.md`.

### Revisions

A Write of a saved plan updates that file: same path, serial, and `created`. The given `status` and `[x]` boxes are kept. A body without frontmatter keeps the saved frontmatter. An Edit of a saved plan is checked against the text it would produce and runs as sent when valid. Never save a revision as a new plan.

### Checkbox grammar

- Open: `[ ]` (space in box required)
- Done: `[x]` (accept `[X]`, write `[x]`)
- Line: `^{id} [ ] {text}$` with optional 0–2 space indent
- `{id}` = `N` / `N.M` / `N.M.K` (digits + dots). **Not** `1. [ ]`. **Not** GitHub `- [ ]`
- Fresh plans: all `[ ]`, never `[x]`
- Marking done: only flip the box. No renumber, delete, or rewrite leaf text
- Depth 2 default (`N` phase + `N.M` leaf). 3rd level only if a leaf would itself be a mini-plan
- Every phase `N` has ≥1 leaf `N.M`. The session agent **executes leaves**. Roll up: all children `[x]` ⇒ parent `[x]`
- Verify = last numbered phase, same grammar
- A Read leaf (``N.M [ ] read `principle-…` ``) sits in the phase it gates, before the leaves it governs. A phase whose every leaf reads a principle gates nothing and is denied on a fresh write: `phase 1 only reads principles; move each read into the phase it gates`. An update is denied only when the saved file had no such phase. Verify reads `principle-prove-it-works` beside its command leaves
- Done plan: every checkbox `[x]`, `status: done`

### Parallel phases

A phase line may end `(parallel: <path>, <path>, …)`, listing every file its leaves write, repo-relative and comma-separated:

```markdown
2 [ ] Parser (parallel: src/parse.ts, src/parse.test.ts)
2.1 [ ] add the parser in src/parse.ts
3 [ ] Printer (parallel: src/print.ts, src/print.test.ts)
3.1 [ ] add the printer in src/print.ts
```

- Adjacent parallel phases form a group whose phases can run at the same time. A group needs two or more phases, and no two of its lists may share a path.
- Paths are compared as written, never resolved on disk; `\` reads as `/`, so `src\cli.ts` and `src/cli.ts` are the same path.
- Denies: `parallel phases 2 and 3 both list src/cli.ts; parallel phases need disjoint files`, `phase 4 is parallel alone; parallel needs two or more adjacent phases`, `phase 2 is parallel with no files; list the files it writes after parallel:`.
- Under a review strategy a group runs at once as `references/review-loop.md` says; `bun repo phase-files <plan> <phases>` checks that each phase wrote only its list.
- Every path a parallel phase's leaves name sits in its list. The save cannot see that; `/review-plan` checks it.

### Prose vs steps

| Section | Amount |
|---|---|
| Goal | 1–3 sentences. What “done” means. |
| Usage | What a person or agent types and sees once the plan lands: each new or changed command, flag, output, error message, or file, in fenced blocks, with the before for each changed one. Internal steps nobody types or reads need none. A plan with no visible change writes one line: `No visible change:` and why. |
| Context / Constraints / Watch-outs | bullets only. Watch-outs: non-obvious footguns; empty allowed (`(none)`). A new plan that names a file a lesson matches cites that lesson path in Watch-outs, or the save is denied. Context includes `Task type:`, `Named checks:` from `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/scope.md` ## Types, and a skip-with-reason when a named check is dropped. |
| Steps | bulk of the file; each leaf = one coherent edit or one file-level action |
| Verify | 1–5 runnable leaves (cmd or observable) |

Tests live in Steps (not a new heading). New behavior or a bug: a failing test leaf before the impl leaf. Other behavior change: a test leaf immediately after the impl leaf. Docs, rename-only, config-only, generated: no test leaf. Verify is the end gate (project cmd or named subset), not a substitute for those leaves. Do not re-run the whole suite after every leaf unless it is cheap.

Thinker cites **repo-relative paths** (`cli/scripts/x.ts`). The plan's worktree `{serial}-{name}` does not exist until the serial is saved, so `/implement-plan-deep` applies each path inside that worktree; an absolute path under the root is accepted too and names the same path there. Leaves must be implementable without re-planning. Product fork → pick the narrowest default, state it under Constraints, still emit steps.

### Validation checklist

- filename matches new stamped regex or legacy unstamped; new writes unpadded + stamp (`1-foo-20260826T143000Z.md` not `0001-foo.md`); serial int equals leading digits; `name` equals slug after stripping optional trailing `-\d{8}T\d{6}Z`
- frontmatter `serial` line matches `^serial: [1-9][0-9]*$` (unpadded decimal ≥ 1; reject `0001`, `"0001"`, `0`, `01`)
- frontmatter keys: `serial`, `name`, `status`, `reviews`, `created`, `source`, `strategy`. `strategy` is optional and is `free`, `spawn-fast` or `spawn-deep`; a save without it takes `agents.defaultStrategy`, else `free`, and another value is invalid. Optional `mode` is `ask`, `auto` or `away`; another value is invalid. `reviews` matches `^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$`, is `0` on a fresh write, is not lowered or removed on an update, and is ≥ 1 for a change into `in-progress`; a legacy plan without it stays valid. Optional `commit:` is a Conventional Commits subject (`type(scope): subject`, scope optional, imperative lowercase, no trailing period). A new plan includes it. A plan with no `commit` key stays valid. A present `commit` that is not that subject is invalid
- `status` ∈ `ready` | `in-progress` | `done` | `blocked`; `created` `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` (new writes) or legacy `YYYY-MM-DD`; `source` ≤120
- headings in order only; no extra `##`; `## Usage` right after `## Goal`, required on a fresh write and optional on an update to a plan saved without it, holding a fenced block or a `No visible change:` line; lines inside code fences are never headings or checkboxes; `## Previous mistakes` last and required on a fresh write, entries valid and append-only on an update; fresh write cites every matched lesson in Watch-outs; no required Why heading (optional footnote only)
- ≥1 `N.M [ ]` leaf; every phase has ≥1 leaf; Verify is last numbered phase
- `PLAN_NAME:` dropped wherever it sits above the first `##` outside a fence
- ≤100 lines above `## Previous mistakes`, frontmatter included; an update over 100 only when no longer than the saved file
- no phase whose every leaf reads a principle, on a fresh write or on an update whose saved file had none
- `(parallel: …)` phases come in adjacent groups of two or more, each with a non-empty list, lists disjoint after `\` → `/`
- checkbox grammar (`N [ ]` / `N.M [ ]` / `N.M.K [ ]`); no `- [ ]`; no `1. [ ]`
- fresh write: the card right after `# {slug}` and one blank line, `WHAT` `WHY` `RISK` `TOUCH` `DONE` in order, padded to 7 columns, text non-empty, each line ≤120 characters; zero `[x]` / `[X]`; Goal 1–3 sentences; Context/Constraints/Watch-outs bullets; Context includes `Task type:`, `Named checks:`, and a skip-with-reason when a named check is dropped; frontmatter includes `commit:` and `strategy:`; Verify 1–5 leaves

### Worked example

File: `.repo/plans/1-notes-export-json-20260826T143000Z.md`

````markdown
---
serial: 1
name: notes-export-json
status: ready
reviews: 0
created: 2026-08-26T14:30:00Z
source: "add --json to notes export"
commit: feat(notes): add --json to notes export
strategy: free
---

# notes-export-json

WHAT   notes export --json prints every note as one JSON array
WHY    scripts read notes without parsing the text table
RISK   an empty notebook must print [], and the table stays the default
TOUCH  src/cli.ts, src/export.ts (+ test)
DONE   bun run test passes; notes export --json | JSON.parse exits 0

## Goal
`notes export --json` prints every note as one JSON array on stdout, so scripts read notes without parsing the text table. The text table stays the default.

## Usage
Before:

```console
$ notes export --json
error: unknown flag --json
```

After:

```console
$ notes export --json
[{"id":1,"title":"groceries","updated":"2026-08-26T14:00:00Z"}]
$ notes export
1  groceries  2026-08-26 14:00
```

## Context
- Task type: feature
- Named checks: failing test before impl; read `principle-test-behavior-not-implementation`
- `/home/dev/Development/example-app/src/cli.ts` parses flags; `/home/dev/Development/example-app/src/export.ts` prints the table
- Rejected: a separate `notes json` command, which splits one export into two

## Constraints
- Keys are `id`, `title`, `updated`, in that order; `updated` is ISO 8601 UTC
- No new dependency

## Watch-outs
- An empty notebook prints `[]`, not nothing

## Steps
1 [ ] Failing test
1.1 [ ] read `principle-test-behavior-not-implementation`
1.2 [ ] in `/home/dev/Development/example-app/src/export.test.ts`, `notes export --json` on two notes prints a two-element array with those keys, and on none prints `[]`
1.3 [ ] run `bun run test export`; the new cases fail on the unknown flag
2 [ ] Implement
2.1 [ ] parse `--json` in `/home/dev/Development/example-app/src/cli.ts`
2.2 [ ] in `/home/dev/Development/example-app/src/export.ts`, print `JSON.stringify` of the notes when `--json` is set
2.3 [ ] run the test from 1.3; all pass

## Verify
3 [ ] Verify
3.1 [ ] read `principle-prove-it-works`
3.2 [ ] `bun run test` passes
3.3 [ ] `notes export --json | node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(0, 'utf8'))"` exits 0

## Previous mistakes
(none)
````

## Review loop

Read this when the plan's `strategy` is `spawn-fast` or `spawn-deep`. You are the reviewer. An implementer agent writes the product code. Values: `plan-format.md`. Gate rules: `hooks.md`.

### Start

The first action, at start or on resume, is a plan save (a status or box edit). It stamps the session. Until it runs, the gate does not know this session reviews.

### Phases

- Phases run in order; each goes to one implementer: `implementer-fast` first on `spawn-fast`, `implementer-deep` on `spawn-deep` (`implementerOf(strategy, 1)`). A parallel group spawns its implementers in one message. Each brief lists its phase's files as the only ones it writes; that list is guidance, and `bun repo phase-files` is the check. A parallel implementer runs only its phase's tests, never `sync` or the full suite. After the round, run `phase-files`, then stage each passed phase by name, one at a time, and run the full suite once. A failed phase reruns alone.
- The brief is that phase's leaves, plus the findings to fix. The agent file holds the rest of its rules. The spawn prompt names the plan's worktree path (`<root>/.worktrees/{serial}-{name}`): a Claude subagent starts in the parent's cwd, the root, where the gate denies a product write. Run `bun repo worktree add {serial}-{name}` first if it is missing.
- A Read leaf in a phase goes to that phase's implementer with the brief: it reads the principle, you do not. You read only `principle-prove-it-works`, before Verify.
- Your own product writes are denied. The plan, the journal and `.tmp/` stay writable.
- Only you tick boxes and write the journal. Write one entry per round.

### Review

- Read the implementer's report: `changed:`, `tests:`, `status:`. A missing report or a status other than `done` is a failed round.
- Read the real `git diff` in the worktree and rerun the phase's tests yourself. Do not trust the report.
- Send findings back to the same implementer. Continue it where the harness allows. Otherwise respawn it with the findings and the current diff.
- A phase passes when the diff matches its leaves and your test run is green.

### Baseline

The index is the baseline. After a phase passes, stage only the implementer's `changed:` files that the phase's leaves name: `git add -- <files>`. Never `git add -A` on this shared tree. The next phase's `git diff` (unstaged) then shows only that phase. The implementer never stages or commits.

### Escalate

After 3 failed rounds, a missing report or a status other than `done`, spawn `implementerOf(strategy, 2)` fresh with the findings. If that one fails the same way, set the plan `blocked` and add a `- blocked:` journal entry.

### Commit

One commit at the end, in the worktree, as `implement-plan-deep` says; `/commit` then runs `finish` from the root. It holds only this plan's files.

### Dumps

You and the implementer send big output through `bun repo job`. The gate rewrites a plain test run to `--job test`. Use `--job exec` for any other large command. Neither of you spawns scout for the implementer's work.

### Not enforced

The gate denies your product writes on claude (Grok runs through it) and codex.

Not enforced on: antigravity, cursor. There, make no product writes yourself; every product edit goes through the implementer.

## Roadmap format (SSOT)

Ordered program of child plans. Not a plan, a handoff, or a design doc.

### Path

`.repo/roadmaps/{serial}-{slug}-{YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ}.md`

- **serial:** unpadded decimal int ≥ 1. Never `0001`.
- **filename:** `^[0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*-\d{8}T\d{6}Z\.md$`
- Create mints the next serial. A later write of an existing file keeps that path and serial. The hook validates the update and the host writes it. An Edit of a saved roadmap is checked against the text it would produce, and a valid one runs as sent.
- Child plans stay in `.repo/plans/`.

### Frontmatter

```yaml
---
serial: 1
name: auth-program
status: draft          # draft | locked | in-progress | done | blocked
reviews: 0             # settled /review-roadmap rounds; never lowered or removed
created: 2026-10-25T18:00:00Z
source: "<≤120 chars>"
strategy: free          # free | spawn-fast | spawn-deep
mode: away             # optional: ask | auto | away
---
```

`draft` → `locked` → `in-progress` → `done` | `blocked`.

`strategy` is optional: `free`, `spawn-fast` or `spawn-deep`. It means what it means in a plan (see `plan-format.md`). On a roadmap it is the default its slices copy: each slice plan starts with the roadmap's value, unless that slice's scope argues for another. A save with no `strategy` gets `agents.defaultStrategy`, else `free`. An unknown value is denied with `strategy: free|spawn-fast|spawn-deep`. A body-only save may send a bare `strategy: {value}` line above `ROADMAP_NAME:`, and a save that omits it keeps the saved value. The person can change the value with a code such as `isf` when approving, or `hsf` when handing off.

`mode` is optional: `ask` or `away`, as in a plan (see `plan-format.md`); the order is the session stamp, then the in-progress `mode`, then `agents.defaultMode`, then `ask`. A body-only save may send a bare `mode: {value}` line above `ROADMAP_NAME:`, and a save that omits it keeps the saved value. Another value is denied with `mode: ask|away`.

`/implement-roadmap-deep` refuses `draft`.

`reviews` counts the `/review-roadmap` rounds whose findings the writer settled. It starts at `0`, never goes down, and once present cannot be removed. A body-only save sends it as a bare `reviews: {n}` line above `ROADMAP_NAME:`, and a save that omits it keeps the saved count. Moving into `locked` needs `reviews` ≥ 1; a missing key counts as 0. A roadmap already past `draft` without the key stays editable.

### Body (this order only)

A roadmap is pointers: what each slice ships, in order. Decisions, Usage, context and the why of each slice go into that slice's plan, which `/implement-roadmap-deep` writes.

```
# auth-program

WHAT   auth ships as two slices: reserved types first, then the commit diff pass
WHY    later slices add skills, so their names must be reserved first
RISK   init and INDEX drift apart when a name changes
TOUCH  init reserved names, INDEX, commit skills
DONE   both slices done; repo init lists auth-types

## Order
1 [ ] auth types: Reserved names list the new skills.
      Location: /home/me/app/.repo/plans/14-auth-types-20261025T165531Z.md
2 [ ] commit diff pass: Commit skills strip narrating comments.

## Verify
3 [ ] Verify
3.1 [ ] both child plans have finished Verify

## Previous mistakes
(none)
```

- **Card:** the 5 lines after `# {slug}` and one blank line, as in a plan (`plan-format.md`): WHAT, WHY, RISK, TOUCH, DONE, text at column 8, at most 120 characters each.
- **Headings:** `## Order`, `## Verify`, `## Previous mistakes`, nothing else. Lines inside a code fence are never headings. A new roadmap with any other `##` is denied with `a new roadmap has only ## Order, ## Verify and ## Previous mistakes; move ## {heading} into the slice plans`.
- **Slice:** one line, `N [ ] {title, 2–6 words}: {one sentence}`. The sentence says what that slice's plan ships. A slice that breaks it is denied with `slice N needs "N [ ] {title, 2–6 words}: {one sentence}"`.
- **Location:** an optional indented line under the slice. Omit it in a draft. `/implement-roadmap-deep` sets it to the absolute plan path `/write-plan-deep` reported; a slice that has one does not get a second plan. A relative `.repo/plans/{file}` also resolves.
- `[x]` only after that child plan's Verify is done.
- **Verify:** 1–5 runnable program gates, same `N.M [ ]` grammar as plans.
- **Previous mistakes:** `(none)`, or one entry per line. Append-only.
- **Cap:** at most 60 lines above `## Previous mistakes`, frontmatter included, `Location:` lines not counted, so filling them in mid-run never trips it. A fresh save past 60 is denied with `{n} lines above ## Previous mistakes, the cap is 60; move detail into the slice plans`; an update only when it grows past both 60 and the saved file.

A roadmap has at least two slices. One slice is `/write-plan-deep`.

#### Roadmaps saved before pointers

A roadmap saved with `## Goal` keeps that shape and its rules for every later save, even one that deletes `## Goal`: the saved file decides. Its headings are `# {slug}`, `## Goal` (1–3 sentences), `## Usage`, `## Context`, `## Decisions`, `## Order`, `## Watch-outs`, `## Verify`, `## Previous mistakes`; Context, Decisions and Watch-outs are bullets, each decision naming the rejected alternative. Each slice is `N [ ] Title: {2–6 words}` with indented `Goal:` (one sentence), `Why:` (one or two sentences) and the optional `Location:`. It has no card and no cap. One saved before `## Usage` or `## Previous mistakes` existed stays valid without them.

### Previous mistakes

Mistakes about the program: slice order, slice boundaries, a premise later slices lean on, and on an old-shape roadmap a Decision that turned out wrong. A mistake inside one slice stays in that child plan.

```
- {feedback|verify|review|premise|decision|slice}: {what was wrong} → {what changed}
- decision: {question} → {choice}, because {why}
```

- `feedback`, `review`, `premise` and `decision` mean what they mean in a plan. `verify` is a failed program Verify gate.
- `slice` is roadmap-only: what child plan N found that changed the Order or a later slice (or a Decision on an old-shape roadmap). The same save makes that change.
- Optional ` (lesson: {slug})` at the end when the entry is also a lesson.
- `/implement-roadmap-deep` copies each entry that touches a slice into that slice's plan Watch-outs, and promotes entries that outlive the program to lessons before `done`.

### Validation checklist

- filename stamped and unpadded; `name` equals the slug
- `status` is one of the five values; `source` ≤120; `strategy` is one of the three values; `mode`, when present, is `ask`, `auto` or `away`
- a new roadmap: the card; only Order, Verify and Previous mistakes, in that order; ≥2 one-line slices, title 2–6 words, one sentence; at most 60 lines above Previous mistakes without `Location:` lines
- an update keeps the saved file's shape; an old-shape one keeps the old checks: headings in order, Goal 1–3 sentences, bulleted Context, Decisions and Watch-outs, ≥2 slices each with Title (2–6 words), one-sentence Goal and Why (1–2 sentences)
- Location, when present, is the absolute plan path (a relative `.repo/plans/{file}` still resolves)
- Verify has 1–5 leaves
- `## Previous mistakes` is last, required on a fresh create, and keeps every saved entry unchanged and in order
- `reviews` is a whole number, never lower than the saved one; `locked` needs at least 1
- a fresh create is `draft`, `reviews: 0`, and has no `[x]`

## RTK

Shell stdout compression. PreToolUse: Bash → `rtk <cmd>`. Not Read/Grep/Glob/prompts/images.

Grok PostToolUse is observe-only — do not attempt output scrub; compress via RTK / spawn / isolation facts only.

### Commands

ls · tree · read · smart · git · gh · glab · clasp · aws · psql · pnpm · err · test · json · deps · env · find · diff · log · dotnet · docker · kubectl · oc · summary · grep · rg · init · wget · wc · gain · cc-economics · config · jest · vitest · prisma · tsc · next · lint · prettier · format · playwright · lightpanda · cargo · npm · npx · curl · discover · session · telemetry · learn · run · proxy · pipe · trust · untrust · verify · ruff · pytest · mypy · rake · rubocop · rspec · pip · go · gt · golangci-lint · gradlew · mvn · hook-audit · rewrite · hook · help

**git:** diff · log · status · show · add · commit · push · pull · branch · fetch · stash (list show pop apply drop push) · worktree
**cargo:** build · test · clippy · check · install · nextest
**go:** test · build · vet
**docker:** ps · images · logs · compose (ps logs build)
**gh:** pr · issue · run · repo
**clasp:** login · logout · create · clone · pull · push · status · open · run · deploy · logs · setting

Flags: `-v`/`-vv`/`-vvv` · `--ultra-compact` · `--skip-env` · `-h` · `-V`

Unknown cmds passthrough. `rtk run` unfiltered.

**playwright:** test-runner family only — not the browser rail.
**lightpanda:** browser-rail CDP via `bun repo browser` (not MCP, not env).

## Scope

Plan by default. A straight shot is the exception. The plan caps the result, so its depth scales with the work. This file is the size-gate SSOT.

### Gate

Straight shot: one file, one obvious edit, nothing to decide. Do it, starting with `bun repo worktree add <name>` like any other change: the main checkout takes no product writes. Also skip planning for questions, lookups, commits, a follow-up inside an approved plan, and an explicit "just do it".

Plan: two or more files, two or more items in the message, two or more valid approaches, cross-cutting or hard-to-undo work, or the user asked to plan. A named goal is not a named edit. "Just" or "should be easy" on a goal is not "just do it": only words that skip the plan itself, such as "just do it" or "no plan", do.

`/ask` is this loop: it stops once for plan approval, then runs to done. It does not skip approval. `/away` decides instead of asking and logs each choice as a `decision` entry; under away the Stop hook runs the approval block's header choice once the review settles and logs it. Any stamp beats a saved `mode: ask|away`, which applies only when the session has no stamp. With no stamp and no in-progress `mode:`, `agents.defaultMode` applies, else `ask`. A fast plan (`/write-plan-fast`, at most 40 lines, no review: `fast-plan-format.md`) or a fast roadmap (`/write-roadmap-fast`, at most 20 lines, no review: `fast-roadmap-format.md`) runs when the person asks for it or when `agents.defaultEffort` is `fast`; otherwise the process here stays the default. `/rn <task>` skips the plan, the review, questions and its own test run, never the worktree or the commit gate.

### Research

Read and search until every leaf is defensible and needs no re-planning. Depth scales with stakes and ambiguity: a clear task needs enough to write the leaves; an unclear, cross-cutting, or hard-to-undo one needs the alternatives checked against the code, docs, and data. Fat notes go under `.repo/scratch/`.

### Questions

Ask only what research cannot settle and what changes the plan's shape: intent, scope, a trade-off the user owns. Batch them into one round, each with your recommendation. Research again on each answer, and ask again only if a new plan-shaping gap appears. When research settles everything, skip this step and write the plan in one shot.

### Plan

`/write-plan-deep`. Format: `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/plan-format.md`. A plan over 100 lines above `## Previous mistakes`, frontmatter included, is a roadmap: split it with `/write-roadmap-deep`. The plan is the proposal: the chosen approach and its rejected alternative sit in Context or Constraints. A minor open choice is written as the default plus "confirm"; a plan-shaping one goes back to Questions. Before writing, run `bun repo lessons match` on the files the plan touches and cite each match in Watch-outs. After saving, run `/review-plan {n}` in a fresh agent, settle each finding, add a `review` entry to `## Previous mistakes` for each one you accept, and bump frontmatter `reviews` in that save. Write `mode:` beside `strategy:` only when the session runs `/away` or the person asked for a mode. Report the goal, phases, top risks, open assumptions and path, then stop with the approval block (`/write-plan-deep` has the full form). The block comes only after the review settled, with `reviews` bumped since the review spawn; the Stop hook blocks it before that.

### Approval

Feedback revises the same plan file (a Write of a saved plan updates it in place) and adds a `feedback` entry to `## Previous mistakes`; research again if needed. Run `/review-plan` again on the revision. Stop again until the user approves. A plan with `reviews: 0` cannot move to `in-progress`; run `/review-plan {n}` first. Approval is the user replying `i` (or a short yes, or a code such as `isf`) to the approval block, an explicit "plan and do it" in the request, or `/implement-roadmap-deep` running a roadmap whose status is `locked` or `in-progress`. A plan-shaping question still stops and leaves that roadmap `locked` or `in-progress`. `h` hands the whole block to a fresh session and keeps each file's strategy; `hf`, `hsf` and `hsd` write `free`, `spawn-fast` or `spawn-deep` first. The hook writes one handoff and names the `/pickup {serial}` to run there; do no work in this session. An `i` or `h` on an item whose review has not settled is refused.

### Implement

`/implement-plan-deep` after approval. Same turn when the request said "plan and do it", or when `/implement-roadmap-deep` is running a `locked` or `in-progress` roadmap. Skip `[x]`. Write-allowlist = paths listed in the plan, repo-relative to that worktree. Do not skip test leaves. Work in the plan's worktree `{serial}-{name}` (`worktree.ts add`). Before the first leaf, check the latest commits and read the plan's `## Previous mistakes`. A failed Verify, a test that failed after a fix, or `principle-attack-the-premise` firing adds a `verify` or `premise` entry. An entry that will happen again on other tasks also becomes a lesson, written in that worktree: `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/lessons.md`. Journal: `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/implementation-format.md` under `.repo/implementations/` (create on start; not for straight shots). Straight shot (`/rn` is exempt from the test and proof steps; the commit hook's gate runs the related tests): run the nearest existing test when the repo has one, repro a bug before the edit, and scaffold a test file only for a bug. Before you call a straight shot done, read `principle-prove-it-works`. Before you ask the user, read `principle-never-block-on-the-human`. Under away, log a `decision` entry instead of asking. Before a large dump or a fan-out, read `principle-guard-the-context-window`.

### Types

One type per plan. Pick the strongest match. A feature that crosses an ownership, package, or API boundary is `cross-cut`. Straight shots skip this table and follow the straight-shot rule in ## Implement. Skip a named check only with a reason in Context. Approval of the plan is the select.

`/write-plan-deep` copies the row into Steps or Verify, including a Read leaf for each named principle. Each Read leaf sits in the phase it gates, not in a phase of its own. `/implement-plan-deep` reads that skill and follows it.

A slice is one child plan, not a phase. Two or more ordered slices are a roadmap (`/write-roadmap-deep`, then `/implement-roadmap-deep`), not one plan. `/write-roadmap-deep` runs `/review-roadmap {n}` in a fresh agent after each save, the same way plans are reviewed, and a roadmap with `reviews: 0` cannot be locked. Format: `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/roadmap-format.md`.

| type | checks |
| --- | --- |
| bug | repro; failing test before impl; read `principle-fix-root-causes`; read `principle-test-behavior-not-implementation` |
| feature | failing test before impl; read `principle-test-behavior-not-implementation` |
| docs | no test leaf; no browser unless the doc is a live page; Verify reads the page or runs the generator |
| perf | Verify states the measurement and what limits it; read `principle-explain-the-number` |
| refactor | existing suite or characterization tests; no feature leaves; read `principle-laziness-protocol`; read `principle-subtract-before-you-add`; read `principle-minimize-reader-load`; read `principle-test-behavior-not-implementation` |
| cross-cut | Context holds architect lite (types, signatures, module map, rejected shape); a `/blast-radius` leaf; read `principle-foundational-thinking`; read `principle-type-system-discipline` |
| chore | no test leaf unless a check already exists |

### Facts

`/write-plan-deep` adds a Read leaf for each fact that is true, in the phase that fact gates. No fact, no leaf. `/implement-plan-deep` reads that skill and follows it.

| fact | read |
| --- | --- |
| a guard, parser, or adapter at a CLI, config, or network edge | `principle-boundary-discipline` |
| a new internal API while old callers still exist | `principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis` |
| a command or loop that must survive crash and retry | `principle-make-operations-idempotent` |
| two actors can write the same file, branch, or key | `principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state` |
| stateful logic, or the same shape copied across files | `principle-model-the-domain` |
| a sweep of similar edits | `principle-build-the-lever` |
| a rewrite with phase boundaries | `principle-outcome-oriented-execution` |
| a person will see the output, the error text, or the default | `principle-experience-first` |
| the requirement does not fit without a special-case branch | `principle-redesign-from-first-principles` |
| research left two or more live options and the choice is hard to undo | `principle-exhaust-the-design-space` |

`/implement-plan-deep` reads a principle only when the type row names it, a true fact names it, the next sentence names it, or an already-read principle cites it. Do not open the rest of the catalog.

Verify of every plan reads `principle-prove-it-works`. After two fixes that share a premise fail the same gate, read `principle-attack-the-premise` before a third try. Before you ask the user, read `principle-never-block-on-the-human`. Before a large dump or a fan-out, read `principle-guard-the-context-window`.

`/write-roadmap-deep` reads `principle-sequence-verifiable-units`. `/correct` reads `principle-encode-lessons-in-structure`.

## Setup

Handheld machine setup for optional integrations. Any OS. Secrets stay in `~/.workerstack/` (Windows `%USERPROFILE%\.workerstack`). Not git. Env still wins over the file.

```
bun repo setup
bun repo setup speak
bun repo setup listen
bun repo setup google-workspace
bun repo setup browser
bun repo setup jev
```

TTY: menu with ok/missing. The menu lists enabled packs and always lists browser and jev. A pack is enabled when `agents.skills` in `repo.config.ts` names it. `bun repo setup <pack>` when that pack is off prints how to enable it (add it to `agents.skills`, then `bun repo sync`) and exits 1. Already ok asks redo (`--redo` skips the ask). Missing bins: print the OS command (never run it), then re-check PATH. Ends with one status line per listed target. Non-TTY needs flags (keys / `--creds`). Doctor never installs bins; setup never installs bins either.

| target | what it writes | flags |
| --- | --- | --- |
| speak | `~/.workerstack/speak.json` | `--elevenlabs-key` `--openai-key` `--provider` `--skip-verify` |
| listen | same file (`openai` / `listen`) plus `~/.workerstack/whisper/` | `--openai-key` `--device` `--skip-download` |
| google-workspace | Desktop OAuth JSON + tokens under `~/.workerstack/` | `--creds PATH` `--account NAME` `--project ID` |
| browser | nothing (print Lightpanda / Chromium hints; both required except win32 Chromium-only) | |
| jev | `~/.workerstack/jev.json` (`apiKey`, mode 0600). `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` wins when set | `--api-key` |

### Full-permission defaults

`bun repo init` and `bun repo yolo` merge full-permission keys into six machine-wide files, keeping every other key (skip with `--skip-globals`). Plain `claude`, `codex`, `grok`, `agy`, `cursor-agent` and `opencode` then start without approval prompts; there are no `repo:<agent>` launch scripts.

| host | dest under `$HOME` | keys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| claude | `.claude/settings.json` | `permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"`, `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt = true` |
| codex | `.codex/config.toml` | `approval_policy = "never"`, `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` |
| grok | `.grok/config.toml` | `[ui] permission_mode = "always-approve"` plus the orchestrator, subagent, memory and `[features]` tables |
| antigravity | `.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` | `toolPermission = "always-proceed"` |
| cursor | `.cursor/cli-config.json` | `approvalMode = "unrestricted"` |

`bun repo yolo` applies by default; `--dry-run` previews, `--check` prints one line of per-host status, exits 1 on any drift, and `--host <id>` limits it to one host; an unknown id prints `unknown host: <id>` and a deleted payload prints `missing payload: <path>`. `bun repo doctor` shows one `globals` row: `ok`, or the first drift line, which names the host, dest and key and ends with the `bun repo yolo` hint. The project hooks (gate-fat-tools, scrub-spawn-prompt) still run in bypass mode.

opencode (V2) has no yolo flag: its payload is one allow-all rule in `permissions` of `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. The merge puts that rule ahead of the rules already there, so a user's own `deny` or `ask` still wins, and a second run adds nothing. A dest whose `permissions` is not a list, or one with an `opencode.jsonc` beside it (the file opencode reads), is left as is: apply prints `skip opencode .config/opencode/opencode.json: <reason>`, `--check` prints `opencode skipped: <reason>` and exits 1.

`bun repo shim` installs a bare `repo` launcher once per machine, so a command runs without the `bun` prefix. It writes a launcher into `~/.local/bin` (Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\workerstack\bin`, with `repo.mjs` and `repo.cmd` beside it for cmd.exe and PowerShell). From any directory the launcher runs the nearest parent's `node_modules/@workerstack/repo`, so each project keeps its own version; outside a project it prints `repo: no @workerstack/repo found above <dir>; run \`bun install\` in the project` and exits 1. `--dry-run` previews, `--check` exits 1 on a missing or stale file, `--dir <path>` installs elsewhere. When the directory is not on PATH it prints the line to add (bash and zsh, fish, or PowerShell); it never edits PATH or a shell rc file. Rerun it after upgrading the package: `bun repo doctor` shows a `shim` row (`ok`, `not installed` or `stale`). bun must be on PATH, as for `bun repo`.

Do not invent keys. If the session is not a TTY, tell the user to run `bun repo setup` in their terminal. This spec is enough. Do not read https://github.com/workerstack/repo#readme unless this file is missing.

## Speak

Text-to-speech from the session. Output only. Not STT. Not a mic. Not MCP. Speech-to-text is `/listen`: `node_modules/@workerstack/repo/references/listen.md` and `bun repo listen`.

```
bun repo speak whoami
bun repo speak voices [--provider elevenlabs|openai]
bun repo speak say --text "hello" [--provider elevenlabs|openai] [--voice ID] [--out path] [--play]
```

`say` writes an mp3 under `.repo/tmp/speak/` (or `--out`) and prints the path. `--play` is local `afplay` (mac) or `ffplay`.

### Auth

Handheld (any OS): `bun repo setup speak` or `bun repo setup` → speak. Opens the key page, hides the paste, writes `~/.workerstack/speak.json`, verifies. Non-TTY: `--elevenlabs-key` / `--openai-key`.

If a key is missing or rejected, the CLI prints `setup: bun repo setup speak` and exits 1. Agents should show that line, not a stack or JSON. Do not invent a key.

One key is enough. Never commit it.

| | env | file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ElevenLabs | `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` | `elevenlabs.apiKey` |
| OpenAI | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `openai.apiKey` |
| Force provider | `SPEAK_PROVIDER` | `provider` |

`~/.workerstack/speak.json` (chmod 600):

```json
{
  "provider": "elevenlabs",
  "elevenlabs": {
    "apiKey": "sk_…",
    "voiceId": "JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb",
    "modelId": "eleven_multilingual_v2"
  },
  "openai": {
    "apiKey": "sk-…",
    "voice": "coral",
    "model": "gpt-4o-mini-tts"
  }
}
```

Env wins over the file. Default provider is `SPEAK_PROVIDER` else the first configured key (elevenlabs, then openai).

### Defaults

- ElevenLabs voice: George `JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb`. Model: `eleven_multilingual_v2`.
- OpenAI voice: `coral`. Model: `gpt-4o-mini-tts`.
- Format: mp3.

Create an ElevenLabs key at https://elevenlabs.io/app/settings/api-keys. OpenAI at https://platform.openai.com/api-keys.

Doctor reports speak as optional: `ok` when a key or `~/.workerstack/speak.json` exists, else `missing (optional)`. It prints the provider name, not the secret.

## Sync

### Skills naming

Do not reuse a repo skill name for a consumer custom skill: a repo-owned skill of the same name in `.repo/skills/` replaces the stock one. Pack names stay reserved when their directory is absent.

`bun repo sync` links the stock skills from the installed package into each host tree and writes the rest; it never copies stock references or scripts. doctor/listen/speak call the consumer's root `scripts/lib/env.mjs` `loadEnv` when that file exists.

Upgrading is running `bun repo update '@workerstack/*'`: it bumps every `@workerstack/*` package to its npm latest, installs, and prints what that install's sync wrote and removed, plus each package's CHANGELOG sections between the installed and the new version. The first sync in a repo an older `bun repo init` copied moves your own rules, subagents, skills, settings keys, lessons, hooks and references into `.repo/` and `references/`, untracks the generated paths, removes the copied `.rulesync/`, and prints one moved line per move. Commit the result.

Each section `bun repo sync` writes below, like its blocks in `.gitignore` and `.gitattributes`, sits between an opening and a closing comment that name it, and the opening one carries a short hash of the text sync wrote. Keep your own lines outside them: a line added or edited inside is moved just below the section by the next sync. A missing, doubled, misplaced or mangled comment is repaired rather than failing sync, each repair printing one line that names the file. A section a new version no longer writes is cut, and a shared file nothing writes any more keeps your lines with its sections cut, removed only when nothing else is left.

### Untracked outputs

In a consumer, sync rebuilds these files from the installed package on every install. The skill links point into `node_modules`. A committed copy drifts from the package and conflicts on each upgrade. So sync keeps them in the `repo:ignore` block of `.gitignore`.

`bun repo sync` and `bun repo sync --check` refuse when git tracks a file the block covers. They print one line per block line, with the `git rm --cached` command to run. Migrate and adopt untrack a committed tree themselves.
